title.zh: 卷一百二十八 列傳第十五: 阿朮 阿里海牙 相威 土土哈
title.en: Volume 128 Biographies 15: Aju, Ariq Qaya, Xiangwei, Tutuha
title.raw: 卷一百二十八 列傳第十五: 阿朮 阿里海牙 相威 土土哈 Volume 128 Biographies 15: Aju, Ariq Qaya, Xiangwei, Tutuha

sentences.zh: 四年八月，觀兵襄陽，遂入南郡，取仙人、鐵城等柵，俘生口五萬。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year, he reviewed troops at Xiangyang, then entered Nan Commandery, took the stockades at Xianren, Tiecheng, and others, and captured fifty thousand living captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year, he mustered his forces at Xiangyang, entered Nan Commandery, seized the stockades at Xianren and Tiecheng among others, and took fifty thousand captives alive.

sentences.zh: 軍還，宋兵邀襄、樊間。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Song troops intercepted them between Xiang and Fan.
translations.idiomatic: On the march back, Song forces ambushed them between Xiangyang and Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 阿術乃自安陽灘濟江，留精騎五千陣牛心嶺，復立虛寨，設疑火。

translations.literal: Aju then crossed the river from Anyang Beach, left five thousand elite horsemen arrayed at Niuxin Ridge, again set up empty camps, and deployed deceptive fires.
translations.idiomatic: Aju crossed the river from Anyang Beach, posted five thousand picked cavalry on Niuxin Ridge, erected dummy camps, and lit decoy fires.

sentences.zh: 夜半，敵果至，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: At midnight the enemy indeed arrived; more than ten thousand heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight the enemy came as expected; more than ten thousand were slain.

sentences.zh: 初，阿術過襄陽，駐馬虎頭山，指漢東白河口曰：「若築壘於此，襄陽糧道可斷也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Aju passed Xiangyang, he halted his horse on Tiger Head Mountain, pointed at the mouth of the Baihe River on the Han's east bank, and said: "If a fort is built here, Xiangyang's grain route can be cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, passing Xiangyang, Aju reined in on Tiger Head Mountain, pointed to the mouth of the Baihe on the east bank of the Han, and said, "Build a fort here and Xiangyang's supply line can be severed."

sentences.zh: 五年，遂築鹿門、新城等堡，繼又築台漢水中，與夾江堡相應，自是宋兵援襄者不能進。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he then built forts at Lumen, Xincheng, and elsewhere; subsequently he also built platforms in the middle of the Han River to correspond with the forts on both banks of the river, and from then on Song troops coming to relieve Xiang could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he built forts at Lumen and Xincheng, then erected platforms midstream in the Han to link the riverbank forts; after that Song relief columns could no longer reach Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，大霖雨，漢水溢，宋將夏貴、範文虎相繼率兵來援，復分兵出入東岸林谷間。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year, great torrential rains fell and the Han overflowed; Song generals Xia Gui and Fan Wenhu successively led troops to relieve the city, again dividing forces to enter and exit among the forests and valleys on the east bank.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the sixth year, heavy rains swelled the Han; Song commanders Xia Gui and Fan Wenhu led successive relief armies, sending detachments through the woods and ravines on the eastern shore.

sentences.zh: 阿術謂諸將曰：「此張虛形，不可與戰，宜整舟師備新堡。」

translations.literal: Aju told the generals: "This is a feint; do not give battle. It is fitting to ready the fleet and guard the new fort."
translations.idiomatic: Aju told his commanders, "This is a diversion—do not engage. Ready the fleet and hold the new fort instead."

sentences.zh: 諸將從之。

translations.literal: The generals followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The generals obeyed.

sentences.zh: 明日，宋兵果趨新堡，大破之，殺溺生擒五千餘人，獲戰船百餘艘。

translations.literal: The next day Song troops indeed rushed toward the new fort; they were routed, with more than five thousand killed, drowned, or captured alive, and over a hundred war vessels taken.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Song army struck the new fort as predicted; Aju crushed them, killing or capturing more than five thousand and seizing over a hundred warships.

sentences.zh: 於是治戰船，教水軍，築圓城，以逼襄陽。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired war vessels, trained the navy, and built a circular city to press Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He then refitted warships, drilled the navy, and built a ring of fortifications to choke Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 文虎復率舟師來救，來興國又以兵百艘侵百丈山，前後邀擊於湍灘，俱敗走之。

translations.literal: Fan Wenhu again led a fleet to the rescue; Lai Xingguo also brought a hundred vessels to raid Baizhang Mountain; intercepting them before and after at Tuan Beach, he defeated and drove them all off.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Wenhu sailed to relieve the city again; Lai Xingguo raided Baizhang Mountain with a hundred ships; Aju intercepted both at Tuan Beach and put them to flight.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，破樊城外郛，增築重圍以逼之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year, the outer wall of Fancheng was broken and heavy encirclements were added to press it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year he breached Fancheng's outer defenses and tightened the siege works.

sentences.zh: 宋裨將張順、張貴裝軍衣百船，自上流入襄陽，阿術攻之，順死，貴僅得入城。

translations.literal: Song lieutenant generals Zhang Shun and Zhang Gui loaded a hundred boats with military supplies and, from upstream, entered Xiangyang; Aju attacked them—Shun died, and Gui barely got into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Song lieutenants Zhang Shun and Zhang Gui ran a hundred supply boats downriver into Xiangyang; Aju attacked—Shun was killed and Gui barely made it inside.

sentences.zh: 俄乘輪船順流東走，阿術與元帥劉整分泊戰船以待，燃薪照江，兩岸如晝，阿術追戰至櫃門關，擒貴，余眾盡死。

translations.literal: Soon afterward they took paddle-wheel boats and fled east downstream; Aju and Marshal Liu Zheng divided their warships and moored to wait, burning fuel to light the river so both banks were bright as day; Aju pursued the battle to Guimen Pass, captured Gui, and the rest all died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Gui fled east in paddle-wheel boats; Aju and Marshal Liu Zheng split their fleet and waited, lighting bonfires until the river shone like day; Aju chased them to Guimen Pass, seized Gui, and wiped out the rest.

sentences.zh: 是年九月，加同平章事。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of that year, he was promoted to Associate Grand Councillor of State.
translations.idiomatic: That September he was made Associate Grand Councillor of State.

sentences.zh: 先是，襄、樊兩城，漢水出其間，宋兵植木江中，聯以鐵鎖，中造浮梁，以通援兵，樊恃此為固。

translations.literal: Earlier, the two cities of Xiang and Fan had the Han flowing between them; Song troops planted timbers in the river, linked them with iron chains, and built a floating bridge in the middle to pass relief troops—Fancheng relied on this as its strength.
translations.idiomatic: Previously the Han ran between Xiangyang and Fancheng; the Song had driven piles into the river, chained them with iron, and spanned a pontoon bridge so relief could cross—Fancheng's defense depended on it.

sentences.zh: 至是，阿術以機鋸斷木，以斧斷鎖，焚其橋，襄兵不能援。

translations.literal: At this time Aju used mechanical saws to cut the timbers, axes to sever the chains, and burned the bridge, so Xiang troops could not relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: Now Aju sawed through the piles, chopped the chains, and burned the bridge, cutting off Xiangyang's aid.

sentences.zh: 十二月，遂拔樊城。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Fancheng was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Fancheng fell.

sentences.zh: 襄守將呂文煥懼而出降。

translations.literal: Xiangyang's defending general Lü Wenhuan, in fear, came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangyang's commander Lü Wenhuan, terrified, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十年七月，奉命略淮東。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the tenth year, he received orders to raid Huaidong.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the tenth year he was ordered to sweep Huaidong.

sentences.zh: 抵揚州城下，宋以千騎出戰，阿術伏兵道左，佯北，宋兵逐之，伏發，擒其騎將王都統。

translations.literal: Arriving below Yangzhou city, the Song sent out a thousand horsemen to fight; Aju hid troops on the left of the road, feigned retreat, the Song troops pursued, the ambush sprang, and the Song cavalry commander Wang Dutong was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Yangzhou, he drew out a thousand Song cavalry; Aju hid men on the roadside, feigned retreat, sprang the ambush, and captured their cavalry commander Wang Dutong.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，入覲，與參政阿里海牙奏請伐宋。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, he entered court audience and, together with Vice Administrator Ariq Qaya, memorialized requesting an attack on Song.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year he appeared at court and, with Vice Administrator Ariq Qaya, petitioned to invade Song.

sentences.zh: 帝命相臣議，久不決。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the chief ministers to deliberate; for a long time no decision was reached.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered his chief ministers to debate the matter, but they could not decide for a long time.

sentences.zh: 阿術進曰：「臣久在行間，備見宋兵弱於往昔，失今不取，時不再來。」

translations.literal: Aju stepped forward and said: "Your servant has long been in the ranks and has fully seen that Song troops are weaker than in former times; if we miss the present moment and do not take them, the time will not come again."
translations.idiomatic: Aju stepped forward and said, "I have been in the field for years and have seen clearly that Song forces are weaker than before; miss this moment and it will not return."

sentences.zh: 帝即可其奏，詔益兵十萬，與丞相伯顏、參政阿里海牙等同伐宋。

translations.literal: The Emperor immediately approved the memorial and decreed an additional hundred thousand troops, to join Chancellor Bayan, Vice Administrator Ariq Qaya, and others in attacking Song together.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder at once approved the petition, added a hundred thousand men, and sent him with Chancellor Bayan, Vice Administrator Ariq Qaya, and others against Song.

sentences.zh: 三月，進平章政事。

translations.literal: In the third month, he was promoted to Grand Councillor of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was promoted to Grand Councillor of State.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，師次郢之鹽山，得俘民言：「宋沿江九郡精銳，盡聚郢江東、西兩城，今舟師出其間，騎兵不得護岸，此危道也。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn the army halted at Yanshan in Ying; from captive civilians they learned: "Song's elite along the nine riverine commanderies are all gathered in Ying's eastern and western cities on the river; if the fleet now passes between them, cavalry cannot protect the banks—this is a perilous route.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn in the ninth month the army stopped at Yanshan in Ying; captives reported that Song's best troops along nine river prefectures were massed in Ying's twin river cities—sending the fleet between them with cavalry unable to shield the banks would be a deadly course.

sentences.zh: 不若取黃家灣堡，東有河口，可由其中拖船入湖，轉以下江為便。」

translations.literal: Better to take Huangjiawan Fort—east of it is a river mouth by which boats can be towed into the lake and then turn downriver, which is convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Better to seize Huangjiawan Fort; east of it a channel leads into the lake and then downriver—a safer path.

sentences.zh: 從之，遂舍攻郢而去。

translations.literal: They followed this and thereupon abandoned the attack on Ying and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed, abandoned the assault on Ying, and marched on.

sentences.zh: 行大澤中，忽宋騎兵千人突至。

translations.literal: Marching through a great marsh, suddenly a thousand Song horsemen burst upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing a great marsh, a thousand Song horsemen suddenly charged.

sentences.zh: 時從騎才數十人，阿術即奮槊馳擊。

translations.literal: At the time his escort numbered only several tens of horsemen; Aju immediately grasped his spear and galloped to attack.
translations.idiomatic: He had only a few dozen riders with him; Aju seized his lance and charged.

sentences.zh: 所向畏避，追斬五百餘級，生擒其將趙、范二統制。

translations.literal: Wherever he went they feared and gave way; pursuing, he cut off more than five hundred heads and captured alive the generals Zhao and Fan, both regimental commanders.
translations.idiomatic: All who faced him gave way; in pursuit he killed more than five hundred and captured the regimental commanders Zhao and Fan alive.

sentences.zh: 進攻沙洋、新城，拔之。

translations.literal: Advancing, he attacked Shayang and Xincheng and took them.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on, stormed Shayang and Xincheng, and captured both.

sentences.zh: 前次復州，守將翟貴迎降。

translations.literal: Moving forward he halted at Fuzhou; the defending general Zhai Gui came out to welcome him and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Fuzhou, the garrison commander Zhai Gui came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 時夏貴鎖大艦扼江、漢口，兩岸備禦堅嚴。

translations.literal: At the time Xia Gui locked great ships to block the Jiang and Hankou; defenses on both banks were stern and tight.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Gui had chained great warships across the Yangtze and Han estuary; both banks were heavily fortified.

sentences.zh: 阿術用軍將馬福計，回舟淪河口，穿湖中，從陽羅堡西沙蕪口入大江。

translations.literal: Aju used the plan of the army officer Ma Fu: turning the boats back to the mouth of the Lun River, cutting through the lake, and entering the great river from Xiwu Pass below Yangluo Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Aju adopted the plan of his officer Ma Fu: double back to the Lun River mouth, thread the lakes, and enter the Yangtze from Xiwu Pass below Yangluo Fort.

sentences.zh: 十二月，軍至陽羅堡，攻之不克。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the army reached Yangluo Fort; attacking it, they could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they reached Yangluo Fort but could not capture it.

sentences.zh: 阿術謂伯顏曰：「攻城，下策也。

translations.literal: Aju told Bayan: "Besieging cities is the inferior stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Aju told Bayan, "Storming walled cities is the worst option.

sentences.zh: 若分軍船之半，循岸西上，對青山磯止泊，伺隙搗虛，可以得志。」

translations.literal: If half the army's ships are divided to follow the shore westward and moor opposite Qingshan Ji, waiting for an opening to strike where the enemy is empty, one can achieve one's aim."
translations.idiomatic: Split the fleet in half, sail up the western shore, and anchor off Qingshan Ji—when a gap opens, strike the weak point and we can succeed."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: They followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan agreed.

sentences.zh: 明日，阿術遙見南岸沙洲，即率眾趨之，載馬後隨。

translations.literal: The next day Aju saw from afar a sandbar on the south bank and immediately led the host toward it, with horses loaded afterward following.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Aju spotted a sandbar on the south bank, led his men toward it, and had the horses ferried after.

sentences.zh: 宋將程鵬飛來拒，大戰中流，鵬飛敗走。

translations.literal: Song General Cheng Pengfei came to resist; a great battle was fought midstream and Pengfei was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Song commander Cheng Pengfei met them; they fought midstream and Pengfei fled in defeat.

sentences.zh: 諸軍抵沙洲，急擊，攀岸步鬥，開而復合者數四，敵小卻，出馬於岸，遂力戰破之，追擊至鄂東門而還。

translations.literal: The armies reached the sandbar and pressed the attack urgently; climbing the bank they fought on foot—opening and closing again four times—the enemy slightly withdrew; horses were brought out onto the bank, and then with full force they broke them, pursuing to the east gate of E and returning.
translations.idiomatic: On the sandbar they stormed ashore; the lines broke and re-formed four times before the enemy gave ground; cavalry came ashore, they broke the Song force, and pursued to Ezhou's east gate before turning back.

sentences.zh: 夏貴聞阿術飛渡，大驚，引麾下兵三百艘先遁，餘皆潰走，遂拔陽羅堡，盡得其軍實。

translations.literal: Xia Gui, hearing that Aju had flown across, was greatly alarmed; leading three hundred of his own vessels he fled first, and the rest all broke and ran; Yangluo Fort was then taken and all its military stores obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Aju had crossed by surprise, Xia Gui panicked, fled first with three hundred ships, and the rest collapsed; Yangluo Fort fell and all its stores were seized.

sentences.zh: 伯顏議師所向，或欲先取蘄、黃，阿術曰：「若赴下流，退無所據，上取鄂、漢，雖遲旬日，師有所依，可以萬全。」

translations.literal: Bayan deliberated where the army should go; some wished first to take Qi and Huang; Aju said: "If we go downstream, on retreat there is nowhere to rely; if we go upstream to take E and Han, though it delays ten days, the army has something to depend on and can be wholly secure."
translations.idiomatic: Bayan debated the army's direction; some favored Qi and Huang first; Aju said, "Downriver we have nowhere to fall back; upriver to E and Han costs ten days but gives us a base and full security."

sentences.zh: 己未，水陸並趨鄂、漢，焚其船三千艘，煙焰漲天，漢陽、鄂州大恐，相繼皆降。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei, by land and water together they rushed toward E and Han, burned three thousand of their ships, smoke and flame filled the sky; Hanyang and Ezhou were greatly terrified and successively all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day land and river forces converged on E and Han, burned three thousand Song ships until smoke blotted the sky; Hanyang and Ezhou surrendered in terror.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，黃、蘄、江州降。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year, Huang, Qi, and Jiangzhou surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year Huangzhou, Qizhou, and Jiangzhou submitted.

sentences.zh: 阿術率舟師趨安慶，範文虎迎降。

translations.literal: Aju led the fleet toward Anqing; Fan Wenhu came out to welcome him and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Aju sailed for Anqing; Fan Wenhu came out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 繼下池州。

translations.literal: He then took Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chizhou fell next.

sentences.zh: 宋丞相賈似道擁重兵拒蕪湖，遣宋京來請和。

translations.literal: Song Chancellor Jia Sidao, holding heavy troops to block Wuhu, sent Song Jing to request peace.
translations.idiomatic: Song Chancellor Jia Sidao, massing a great army at Wuhu, sent Song Jing to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 伯顏謂阿術曰：「有詔令我軍駐守，何如？」

translations.literal: Bayan told Aju: "There is an edict ordering our army to halt and garrison—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Bayan asked Aju, "We have orders to halt and garrison—what do you say?"

sentences.zh: 阿術曰：「若釋似道而不擊，恐已降州郡今夏難守，且宋無信，方遣使請和，而又射我軍船，執我邏騎。

translations.literal: Aju said: "If we release Sidao and do not strike, I fear the prefectures already surrendered will be hard to hold this summer; moreover Song has no trust—just as they send envoys to sue for peace, they also shoot at our ships and seize our patrol riders.
translations.idiomatic: Aju replied, "Spare Sidao and we may lose the prefectures we've taken this summer; Song is faithless—they sue for peace while shooting our ships and seizing our scouts.

sentences.zh: 今日惟當進兵，事若有失，罪歸於我。」

translations.literal: Today we should only advance the army; if anything goes wrong, the blame falls on me."
translations.idiomatic: We must press on; if anything goes wrong, blame me."

sentences.zh: 二月辛酉，師次丁家洲，遂與宋前鋒孫虎臣對陣。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou of the second month the army halted at Dingjiazhou and thereupon faced the Song vanguard Sun Huchen in battle array.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day in the second month the army reached Dingjiazhou and formed battle lines against Song vanguard Sun Huchen.

sentences.zh: 夏貴以戰艦二千五百艘橫亙江中，似道將兵殿其後。

translations.literal: Xia Gui with two thousand five hundred warships stretched across the river; Sidao led troops bringing up the rear.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Gui lined twenty-five hundred warships across the river; Sidao commanded the rear.

sentences.zh: 時已遣騎兵夾岸而進，兩岸樹砲，擊其中堅，宋軍陣動，阿術挺身登舟，手自持柂，突入敵陣，諸軍繼進，宋兵遂大潰。

translations.literal: At the time cavalry had already been sent to advance along both banks; on both banks trebuchets were set up to strike the center; the Song army's formation moved; Aju himself stepped onto a boat, personally held the rudder, burst into the enemy formation, the armies followed in, and the Song troops were then utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry already flanked both banks; trebuchets on shore hammered the Song center; as their line wavered Aju boarded a ship, took the helm himself, drove into the enemy, and the host followed until the Song army collapsed.

sentences.zh: 以上詳見《伯顏傳》。

translations.literal: The above is treated in detail in the Biography of Bayan.
translations.idiomatic: The foregoing is covered in detail in Bayan's biography.

sentences.zh: 世祖以宋重兵皆駐揚州，臨安倚之為重，四月，命阿術分兵圍守揚州。

translations.literal: The Founder, because Song's heavy troops were all stationed at Yangzhou and Lin'an relied on them as its weight, in the fourth month ordered Aju to divide troops to surround and hold Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai, knowing Song's main forces held Yangzhou on which Lin'an depended, ordered Aju in the fourth month to detach troops and invest Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚申，次真州，敗宋兵於珠金砂，斬首二千餘級。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen he halted at Zhenzhou, defeated Song troops at Zhujinsha, and cut off more than two thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day he reached Zhenzhou, routed Song forces at Zhujinsha, and took more than two thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 既抵揚州，乃造樓櫓戰具於瓜洲，漕粟於真州，樹柵以斷其糧道。

translations.literal: Having reached Yangzhou, he then built tower-shields and siege equipment at Guazhou, transported grain from Zhenzhou, and planted palisades to cut off their grain route.
translations.idiomatic: At Yangzhou he built siege towers at Guazhou, shipped grain from Zhenzhou, and threw up barriers to sever their supplies.

sentences.zh: 宋都統姜才領步騎二萬來攻柵，敵軍夾河為陣，阿術麾騎士渡河擊之，戰數合，堅不能卻。

translations.literal: Song regimental commander Jiang Cai led twenty thousand infantry and cavalry to attack the palisades; the enemy army formed battle lines on both sides of the river; Aju commanded horsemen to cross the river and strike them; they fought several engagements but could not be driven back.
translations.idiomatic: Song commander Jiang Cai attacked the barriers with twenty thousand foot and horse; the enemy lined both banks of the river; Aju's cavalry crossed and fought several rounds but could not break them.

sentences.zh: 眾軍佯北，才逐之，遂奮而回擊，萬矢雨集，才軍不能支，擒其副將張林，斬首萬八千級。

translations.literal: The host feigned retreat; Cai pursued; they then turned fiercely to counterattack; ten thousand arrows fell like rain; Cai's army could not hold; his lieutenant Zhang Lin was captured and eighteen thousand heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Aju feigned retreat; Cai pursued; they wheeled and counterattacked; arrows fell like rain; Cai's army broke; lieutenant Zhang Lin was taken and eighteen thousand were slain.

sentences.zh: 七月庚午，宋兩淮鎮將張世傑、孫虎臣以舟師萬艘駐焦山東，每十船為一舫，聯以鐵鎖，以示必死。

translations.literal: On the day gengwu of the seventh month, Song's Huai and Yang garrison commanders Zhang Shijie and Sun Huchen with ten thousand vessels stationed east of Jiaoshan; every ten ships were made one great barge, linked with iron chains, to show they would fight to the death.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day in the seventh month Zhang Shijie and Sun Huchen anchored ten thousand ships east of Jiaoshan, chaining ten vessels into one floating fortress to show they would die fighting.

sentences.zh: 阿術登石公山，望之，舳艫連接，旌旗蔽江，曰：「可燒而走也。」

translations.literal: Aju ascended Shigong Mountain and looked at them; the ships were connected stem to stern, banners and flags covered the river; he said: "They can be burned and driven off."
translations.idiomatic: From Shigong Mountain Aju saw the fleet linked stem to stern, banners blotting the river, and said, "Burn them and they'll run."

sentences.zh: 遂選強健善射者千人，載以巨艦，分兩翼夾射，阿術居中，合勢進擊，繼以火矢燒其蓬檣，煙焰漲天。

translations.literal: He then selected a thousand strong, healthy, skilled archers, loaded them on great ships, divided into two wings to shoot from both sides; Aju was in the center; joining strength they pressed the attack, then followed with fire arrows to burn their sails and masts; smoke and flame filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: He picked a thousand crack archers on great ships, flanked them from both sides, led the center himself, then loosed fire arrows into sails and masts until smoke filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 宋兵既碇舟死戰，至是欲走不能，前軍爭赴水死，後軍散走。

translations.literal: Song troops had already moored their boats to fight to the death; at this point they wished to flee but could not; the front army competed to rush into the water and die; the rear army scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Song had moored to fight to the death; now they could not escape; the van leapt into the water to drown while the rear fled.

sentences.zh: 追至圌山，獲黃鵠白鷂船七百餘艘，自是宋人不復能軍矣。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Tuanshan, they obtained more than seven hundred huang'e and bai'yao boats; from then on the Song people could no longer field an army.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuit reached Tuanshan; they captured more than seven hundred huang'e and bai'yao vessels; after that Song could no longer muster a field army.

sentences.zh: 十月，詔拜中書左丞相，仍諭之曰：「淮南重地，李庭芝狡詐，須卿守之。」

translations.literal: In the tenth month an edict appointed him Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat and still instructed him: "Huainan is a vital region; Li Tingzhi is cunning—you must guard it."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he was named Left Chancellor of the Central Secretariat with the charge: "Huainan is critical; Li Tingzhi is treacherous—you must hold it."

sentences.zh: 時諸軍進取臨安，阿術駐兵瓜洲，以絕揚州之援。

translations.literal: At the time the armies were advancing to take Lin'an; Aju garrisoned troops at Guazhou to cut off Yangzhou's relief.
translations.idiomatic: While other armies marched on Lin'an, Aju held Guazhou to block relief from Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 伯顏所以兵不血刃而平宋者，阿術控制之力為多。

translations.literal: The reason Bayan was able to pacify Song without blood on the soldiers' blades was largely due to Aju's power of control.
translations.idiomatic: That Bayan subdued Song with so little bloodshed owed much to Aju's grip on the theater.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，夏貴舉淮西諸城來附。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year, Xia Gui brought all the cities of Huaidong West to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the thirteenth year Xia Gui surrendered the Huaidong West prefectures.

sentences.zh: 阿術謂諸將曰：「今宋已亡，獨庭芝未下，以外助猶多故也。

translations.literal: Aju told the generals: "Now Song is already destroyed; only Tingzhi is not yet taken, because outside aid is still plentiful.
translations.idiomatic: Aju told his commanders, "Song is gone; only Tingzhi still holds out because outside help remains.

sentences.zh: 若絕其聲援，塞彼糧道，尚恐東走通、泰，逃命江海。」

translations.literal: If we cut off their vocal support and block their grain routes, we still fear they will flee east through Tong and Tai and escape their lives on the rivers and seas."
translations.idiomatic: Cut their reinforcements and grain and they may still slip east through Tongzhou and Taizhou to the sea."

sentences.zh: 乃柵揚之西北丁村，以扼其高郵、寶應之饋運；

translations.literal: He then palisaded Ding Village northwest of Yangzhou to choke their grain transport from Gaoyou and Baoying;
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Ding Village northwest of Yangzhou to choke supplies from Gaoyou and Baoying;

sentences.zh: 貯粟灣頭堡，以備捍禦；

translations.literal: stored grain at Wantou Fort to prepare for defense;
translations.idiomatic: stockpiled grain at Wantou Fort for defense;

sentences.zh: 留屯新城，以逼泰州。

translations.literal: and left troops garrisoned at Xincheng to press Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: and garrisoned Xincheng to press Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 又遣千戶伯顏察兒率甲騎三百助灣頭兵勢，且戒之曰：「庭芝水路既絕，必從陸出，宜謹備之。

translations.literal: He also sent Thousand-Commander Bayanchar with three hundred armored horsemen to reinforce Wantou's military strength, and moreover warned them: "Tingzhi's water route is already cut; he must come out by land—you should guard carefully.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Thousand-Commander Bayanchar with three hundred armored horse to stiffen Wantou, warning them, "Tingzhi's river line is severed; he must break out by land—guard well.

sentences.zh: 如丁村烽起，當首尾相應，斷其歸路。」

translations.literal: If the beacon at Ding Village rises, you should respond head and tail together and cut off their route of return."
translations.idiomatic: If Ding Village's beacon fires, coordinate front and rear and cut off their retreat."

sentences.zh: 六月甲戌，姜才知高郵米運將至，果夜出步騎五千犯丁村柵。

translations.literal: On the day jiaxu of the sixth month, Jiang Cai, learning that Gaoyou's grain transport was about to arrive, indeed by night led five thousand infantry and cavalry to attack Ding Village's palisade.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day in the sixth month Jiang Cai, hearing Gaoyou grain was near, led five thousand foot and horse by night against Ding Village.

sentences.zh: 至曉，伯顏察兒來援，所將皆阿術牙下精兵，旗幟畫雙赤月。

translations.literal: By dawn Bayanchar came to the rescue; those he led were all elite troops under Aju's personal command; on the banners were painted twin red moons.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Bayanchar arrived with Aju's personal guard, their banners marked with twin red moons.

sentences.zh: 眾軍望其塵，連呼曰：「丞相來矣！」

translations.literal: The armies, seeing their dust, repeatedly shouted: "The Chancellor has come!"
translations.idiomatic: Seeing their dust, the troops cried again and again, "The Chancellor is here!"

sentences.zh: 宋軍識其旗，皆遁，才脫身走，追殺騎兵四百，步卒免者不滿百人。

translations.literal: Song troops, recognizing their banners, all fled; Cai alone escaped with his body; pursuing, they killed four hundred horsemen, and of the infantry who were spared not a hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: The Song recognized the banners and fled; only Cai escaped; pursuit killed four hundred horse and left fewer than a hundred foot alive.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，李庭芝以硃煥守揚州，挾姜才東走。

translations.literal: On the day renchen, Li Tingzhi left Zhu Huan to hold Yangzhou and, taking Jiang Cai, fled east.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen day Li Tingzhi left Zhu Huan in Yangzhou and fled east with Jiang Cai.

sentences.zh: 阿術率兵追襲，殺步卒千人，庭芝僅入泰州，遂築壘以守之。

translations.literal: Aju led troops in pursuit and attack, killed a thousand infantry, Tingzhi barely entered Taizhou, and then built fortifications to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Aju pursued, killed a thousand foot soldiers; Tingzhi barely reached Taizhou and threw up defenses.

sentences.zh: 七月乙巳，硃煥以揚州降。

translations.literal: On the day yisi of the seventh month, Zhu Huan surrendered Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the seventh month Zhu Huan surrendered Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，泰州守將孫良臣開北門納降，執李庭芝、姜才，奉命戮揚州市。

translations.literal: On the day yimao, Taizhou's defending general Sun Liangchen opened the north gate to admit surrender, seized Li Tingzhi and Jiang Cai, and by order executed them in Yangzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day Taizhou commander Sun Liangchen opened the north gate, handed over Li Tingzhi and Jiang Cai, and they were executed in Yangzhou by order.

sentences.zh: 揚、泰既下，阿術申嚴士卒，禁暴掠。

translations.literal: After Yang and Tai were taken, Aju strictly ordered the soldiers and forbade violent plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yangzhou and Taizhou fell, Aju strictly forbade looting.

sentences.zh: 有武衛軍校掠民二馬，即斬以徇。

translations.literal: There was a Guard officer of the Martial Guard who plundered two horses from the people; he was immediately beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: A guards officer who seized two civilian horses was beheaded on the spot as an example.

sentences.zh: 兩淮悉平，得府二、州二十二、軍四、縣六十七。

translations.literal: Both Huai regions were entirely pacified; they obtained two prefectures, twenty-two subprefectures, four armies, and sixty-seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: Both sides of the Huai were pacified: two prefectures, twenty-two subprefectures, four armies, and sixty-seven counties.

sentences.zh: 九月辛酉，入見世祖於大明殿，陳宋俘。

translations.literal: On the day xinyou of the ninth month, he entered audience with the Founder in the Hall of Great Brightness and presented Song captives.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day in the ninth month he appeared before Kublai in the Hall of Great Brightness and presented Song captives.

sentences.zh: 第功行賞，實封泰興縣二千戶。

translations.literal: Merits were ranked and rewards distributed; his actual fief was set at two thousand households in Taixing County.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards were apportioned by merit; he received a fief of two thousand households in Taixing County.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，受命北伐叛王昔剌木等。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he received orders for a northern campaign against the rebel princes Xilamu and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was ordered north against the rebel princes Xilamu and others.

sentences.zh: 明年凱旋。

translations.literal: The next year he returned in triumph.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he returned victorious.

sentences.zh: 繼又西征，至哈剌霍州，以疾卒，年五十四，追封河南王。

translations.literal: Subsequently he again campaigned west, reached Halahuo Prefecture, and died of illness at age fifty-four; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned west again, reached Halahuo Prefecture, and died of illness at fifty-four; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: ○阿里海牙

translations.literal: ○ Ariq Qaya
translations.idiomatic: ○ Ariq Qaya

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙，畏吾兒人也。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya was a man of the Uighurs.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya was a Uighur.

sentences.zh: 初生，胞中剖而出。

translations.literal: At birth he was cut out of the womb.
translations.idiomatic: He was born by caesarean section.

sentences.zh: 其父以為不祥，將棄之，母不忍。

translations.literal: His father considered this inauspicious and was about to abandon him; his mother could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: His father took this as an ill omen and meant to abandon him; his mother would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 比長，果聰辨，有膽略。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he indeed proved clever and discerning, with courage and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he proved sharp-witted, brave, and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 家貧，嘗躬耕，舍耒嘆曰：「大丈夫當立功朝廷，何至效細民事畎畝乎！」

translations.literal: The family was poor; he once plowed with his own hands, set down the plow and sighed: "A great man should establish merit at court—why stoop to petty matters like tilling fields!"
translations.idiomatic: Poor as he was, he once plowed himself, laid down the plow, and sighed, "A true man should serve the throne—not waste his life in the furrow!"

sentences.zh: 去，求其國書讀之，逾月，又棄去。

translations.literal: He left, sought out his nation's books and read them; after a month he abandoned that too.
translations.idiomatic: He left home, studied his people's literature, and after a month abandoned that as well.

sentences.zh: 用薦者得事世祖於潛邸。

translations.literal: Through recommendation he came to serve the Founder at the Hidden Residence.
translations.idiomatic: By recommendation he entered Kublai's service while the Founder was still heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，漸見擢用，由左右司郎中遷參議中書省事。

translations.literal: When the Founder ascended the throne, he was gradually promoted and employed, from Left and Right Department Director to Participant in the Affairs of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai took the throne he rose steadily from Left and Right Department Director to Participant in Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，立諸路行中書省，進僉河南行省事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan, Branch Secretariats for all routes were established; he was promoted to Associate Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2, when branch secretariats were established for all circuits, he became Associate Administrator of the Henan branch.

sentences.zh: 五年，命與元帥阿術、劉整取襄陽，又加參知政事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was ordered, together with Marshal Aju and Liu Zheng, to take Xiangyang; he was further made Vice Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was ordered with Marshal Aju and Liu Zheng to take Xiangyang and was made Vice Administrator.

sentences.zh: 始，帝遣諸將，命毋攻城，但圍之，以俟其自降。

translations.literal: At the start the Emperor sent the generals with orders not to assault the city but only to surround it, to await its voluntary surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Emperor told the generals not to storm the city but only to invest it until it surrendered.

sentences.zh: 乃築長圍，起萬山，包百丈、楚山，盡鹿門，以絕之。

translations.literal: They then built a long encirclement from Wanshan, wrapping Baizhang and Chushan, reaching to Lumen, to cut it off.
translations.idiomatic: They built a long siege line from Wanshan, wrapping Baizhang and Chushan through to Lumen, to isolate the city.

sentences.zh: 宋兵入援者皆敗去。

translations.literal: Song troops entering to relieve were all defeated and driven off.
translations.idiomatic: Every Song relief column was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 然城中糧儲多，圍之五年，終不下。

translations.literal: Yet grain stores in the city were plentiful; besieging it for five years, in the end it would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the city held ample grain; five years of siege could not bring it down.

sentences.zh: 九年三月，破樊城外郛，其將復閉內城守。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year the outer wall of Fancheng was broken; its generals again closed the inner city and held it.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year Fancheng's outer wall fell; its garrison withdrew into the inner city.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙以為襄陽之有樊城，猶齒之有脣也，宜先攻樊城，樊城下，則襄陽可不攻而得。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya thought that Fancheng to Xiangyang was like lips to teeth—it was fitting first to attack Fancheng; when Fancheng fell, Xiangyang could be obtained without attack.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya argued that Fancheng was to Xiangyang as lips to teeth—take Fancheng first and Xiangyang would fall without a fight.

sentences.zh: 乃入奏。

translations.literal: He then entered to memorialize.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the court.

sentences.zh: 帝始報可。

translations.literal: The Emperor at first replied that it was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor initially approved.

sentences.zh: 會有西域人亦思馬因獻新砲法，因以其人來軍中。

translations.literal: There happened to be a man from the Western Regions, Ismail, who presented a new method for cannon; accordingly that man was brought to the army.
translations.idiomatic: An West Asian named Ismail offered a new artillery method, and he was brought to the army.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，為砲攻樊，破之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year they used cannon to attack Fan and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year they bombarded Fancheng with cannon and took it.

sentences.zh: 先是，宋兵為浮橋以通襄陽之援，阿里海牙發水軍焚其橋，襄援不至，城乃拔。

translations.literal: Earlier Song troops had built a floating bridge to pass relief to Xiangyang; Ariq Qaya sent the navy to burn the bridge, Xiang relief did not arrive, and the city was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: The Song had bridged the river to relieve Xiangyang; Ariq Qaya's fleet burned the bridge, aid never came, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 詳具《阿術傳》。

translations.literal: Details are fully set forth in the Biography of Aju.
translations.idiomatic: Details appear in Aju's biography.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙既破樊，移其攻具以向襄陽。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya, having broken Fan, moved his siege engines toward Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Fancheng fell, Ariq Qaya turned his siege engines on Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 一砲中其譙樓，聲如雷霆，震城中。

translations.literal: One shot struck the gate tower; the sound was like thunder and shook the city.
translations.idiomatic: One shot hit the gate tower with a thunderous roar that shook the city.

sentences.zh: 城中洶洶，諸將多逾城降者。

translations.literal: Inside the city there was uproar; many generals crossed the wall to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread inside; many officers climbed down and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 劉整欲立碎其城，執文煥以快其意。

translations.literal: Liu Zheng wished to raze the city to fragments and seize Wenhuan to satisfy his mind.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zheng wanted to smash the city and seize Wenhuan for his own satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙獨不欲攻，乃身至城下，與文煥語曰：「君以孤軍城守者數年，今飛鳥路絕，主上深嘉汝忠。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya alone did not wish to attack; he himself came below the city wall and spoke with Wenhuan: "You, with a lone army, have held the city for several years; now even birds' paths are cut off; the sovereign deeply commends your loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya alone opposed storming the walls; he came beneath the gate and told Wenhuan, "You held out for years with a lone garrison; now even birds cannot enter; the sovereign honors your loyalty.

sentences.zh: 若降，則尊官厚祿可必得，決不殺汝也。」

translations.literal: If you surrender, then honored office and rich stipend can surely be obtained; I will absolutely not kill you."
translations.idiomatic: Surrender and high rank and rich stipends are yours—I swear not to harm you."

sentences.zh: 文煥狐疑未決。

translations.literal: Wenhuan hesitated in doubt and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Wenhuan wavered, unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 又折矢與之誓，如是者數四，文煥感而出降。

translations.literal: Again he broke arrows and swore with him; doing this four times, Wenhuan was moved and came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He broke arrows in oath again and again—four times—until Wenhuan was moved and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂與入朝。

translations.literal: He then accompanied him to court audience.
translations.idiomatic: He escorted Wenhuan to court.

sentences.zh: 帝以文煥為昭勇大將軍、侍衛親軍都指揮使、襄漢大都督；

translations.literal: The Emperor made Wenhuan General of Brilliant Courage, Commander-in-Chief of the Palace Guard, and Grand Commander of Xiang and Han;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor made Wenhuan General of Brilliant Courage, Commander of the Palace Guard, and Grand Commander of Xiang and Han;

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙行荊湖等路樞密院事，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya acted as Military Affairs Commissioner for Jinghu and other circuits and garrisoned Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya became Military Affairs Commissioner for Jinghu and garrisoned Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙奏曰：「襄陽自昔用武之地也，今天助順而克之，宜乘勝順流長驅，宋可必平。」

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya memorialized: "Xiangyang from old has been a place where armies were used; today Heaven assisted the righteous and it was taken—it is fitting to ride the victory downstream in a long drive; Song can surely be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya memorialized, "Xiangyang has always been a battlefield; Heaven helped us take it—strike downstream while victory is hot and Song will surely fall."

sentences.zh: 平章阿術亦贊其說。

translations.literal: Associate Grand Councillor Aju also endorsed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Grand Councillor Aju seconded him.

sentences.zh: 帝命丞相史天澤議之。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Chancellor Shi Tianze to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Chancellor Shi Tianze to weigh the plan.

sentences.zh: 天澤曰：「朝廷若遣重臣，如丞相安童、同知樞密院事伯顏者一人，都督諸軍，則四海混同，可立待也。」

translations.literal: Tianze said: "If the court sends a heavy minister—such as Chancellor Antong or Vice Military Affairs Commissioner Bayan—one man to command all armies, then the four seas can be united and one may stand and wait for it."
translations.idiomatic: Tianze said, "Send a senior minister—Chancellor Antong or Vice Military Affairs Commissioner Bayan—to command all forces, and unification of the realm will follow swiftly."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「伯顏可。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Bayan will do."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Bayan will do."

sentences.zh: 乃大徵兵，拜伯顏為行中書省左丞相，阿術為平章。

translations.literal: A great levy of troops was then made; Bayan was appointed Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat and Aju Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: A great levy followed; Bayan became Left Chancellor of the Branch Secretariat and Aju Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙進行省右丞，賞鈔二百錠。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya was promoted to Right Vice Administrator of the Branch Secretariat and rewarded with two hundred ingots of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya was made Right Vice Administrator of the Branch Secretariat and rewarded with two hundred ingots of paper money.

sentences.zh: 十一年九月，會師襄陽，遂破郢州及沙洋、新城。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eleventh year the armies joined at Xiangyang and then broke Ying Prefecture and Shayang and Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eleventh year the armies united at Xiangyang and took Ying Prefecture, Shayang, and Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 十二月，師出沙蕪口。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the army issued from Shaxu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the army marched out through Shaxu Pass.

sentences.zh: 宋制置夏貴守諸隘，甚固。

translations.literal: Song Pacification Commissioner Xia Gui guarded the passes—very firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Song Pacification Commissioner Xia Gui held the passes with great strength.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙麾兵攻武磯堡，貴趨援之。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya waved troops to attack Wuji Fort; Gui rushed to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya assaulted Wuji Fort; Xia Gui hurried to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 阿術遂以兵西渡青山磯，宋都統程鵬飛來迎戰，敗之江中。

translations.literal: Aju then with troops crossed west at Qingshan Ji; Song Regimental Commander Cheng Pengfei came to meet battle and was defeated on the river.
translations.idiomatic: Aju crossed west at Qingshan Ji; Song commander Cheng Pengfei met him and was beaten on the river.

sentences.zh: 會貴兵亦敗走廬州，宣撫硃禩孫夜遁還江陵，知鄂州張晏然以城降，鵬飛以本軍降。

translations.literal: Just then Gui's troops also were defeated and fled to Luzhou; Pacification Commissioner Zhu Yisun fled by night back to Jiangling; Ezhou Prefect Zhang Yiran surrendered the city; Pengfei surrendered with his army.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Gui's force was also routed to Luzhou; Pacification Commissioner Zhu Yisun fled by night to Jiangling; Ezhou Prefect Zhang Yiran surrendered; Pengfei submitted with his army.

sentences.zh: 伯顏與諸將會鄂城下，議曰：「鄂襟山帶江，江南之要區也，且兵糧皆備。

translations.literal: Bayan, with the generals assembled below E City, deliberated: "E embraces mountains and girds the river—it is a vital region of the lands south of the Yangtze, and moreover troops and grain are all prepared.
translations.idiomatic: Bayan and his generals met below Ezhou and debated: "Ezhou commands mountains and river—the key to the south—and its stores are full.

sentences.zh: 今蜀、江陵、岳、鄂皆未下，不以一大將鎮撫之，上流一動，則鄂非我有也。」

translations.literal: Now Shu, Jiangling, Yue, and E are all not yet taken; if a great general is not sent to pacify and reassure them, once the upper reaches stir, then E will not be ours."
translations.idiomatic: Shu, Jiangling, Yue, and E still hold out; without a senior commander to pacify the upper Yangtze, one move upstream and we lose Ezhou."

sentences.zh: 乃以兵四萬遣阿里海牙戍鄂，而與阿術將大兵以東。

translations.literal: Forty thousand troops were then sent with Ariq Qaya to garrison E, while he and Aju led the great army east.
translations.idiomatic: He detached forty thousand men under Ariq Qaya to hold Ezhou and marched east with Aju.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙集鄂民，宣上德惠，禁將士毋侵掠。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya gathered the people of E and proclaimed the sovereign's virtue and grace, forbidding the generals and soldiers from plundering.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya rallied the people of Ezhou, proclaimed the Emperor's mercy, and forbade looting.

sentences.zh: 其下恐懼，無敢取民之菜者，民大悅。

translations.literal: His subordinates were in fear and none dared take the people's vegetables; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: His men were so afraid none would touch a villager's greens; the people rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 遣人徇壽昌、信陽、德安諸郡，皆下。

translations.literal: He sent men to announce Shouchang, Xinyang, De'an, and other commanderies—all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He sent heralds to Shouchang, Xinyang, De'an, and other prefectures—all submitted.

sentences.zh: 進徇江陵。

translations.literal: Advancing, he marched on Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 十有二年春三月，與安撫高世傑兵遇巴陵，命張榮實搗其中堅，解汝楫率諸翼兵左右角之。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring of the twelfth year he met Pacification Commissioner Gao Shijie's troops at Baling; he ordered Zhang Rongshi to strike their center and Xie Ruji to lead wing troops to angle them on left and right.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the twelfth year he met Pacification Commissioner Gao Shijie at Baling; Zhang Rongshi smashed the center while Xie Ruji flanked from both sides.

sentences.zh: 世傑敗走，追降之於桃花灘。

translations.literal: Shijie was defeated and fled; pursuing, he surrendered him at Taohua Beach.
translations.idiomatic: Shijie fled; pursuit caught him at Taohua Beach and he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 遂下岳州。

translations.literal: Yue Prefecture was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 四月，至沙市，城不下，縱火攻之，沙市立破，宣撫硃禩孫、制置高達恐即以城降。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he reached Shashi; the city would not fall; setting fire to attack it, Shashi was immediately broken; Pacification Commissioner Zhu Yisun and Pacification Commissioner Gao Da, in terror, immediately surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he reached Shashi; when the city resisted he burned it down; Zhu Yisun and Gao Da surrendered in terror.

sentences.zh: 乃入江陵，釋系囚，放戍券軍，除其徭賦及法令之繁細者。

translations.literal: Entering Jiangling, he released bound prisoners, freed garrison-ticket troops, and removed their corvée labor and the fine points of laws and orders.
translations.idiomatic: Entering Jiangling he freed prisoners and garrison conscripts and lightened taxes and petty regulations.

sentences.zh: 傳檄郢、歸、峽、常德、澧、隨、辰、沅、靖、復、均、房、施、荊門及諸洞，無不降者。

translations.literal: Proclamations were sent to Ying, Gui, Xia, Changde, Li, Sui, Chen, Yuan, Jing, Fu, Jun, Fang, Shi, Jingmen, and the various mountain caves—none did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Proclamations went to Ying, Gui, Xia, Changde, Li, Sui, Chen, Yuan, Jing, Fu, Jun, Fang, Shi, Jingmen, and the hill tribes—none refused submission.

sentences.zh: 盡奏官其所降官，以兵守峽，籍其戶口財賦來上。

translations.literal: He fully memorialized to appoint officials for those who surrendered, sent troops to guard the gorges, and registered households, wealth, and taxes to report upward.
translations.idiomatic: He reported all surrendered officials for appointment, garrisoned the gorges, and registered households and revenue for the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝喜，大宴三日，語近臣曰：「伯顏兵東，阿里海牙以孤軍戍鄂，朕甚憂之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased, held a great banquet for three days, and told close ministers: "Bayan's army goes east; Ariq Qaya with a lone army garrisons E—I was very worried.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rejoiced, feasted three days, and told his intimates, "Bayan marched east while Ariq Qaya held E alone—I feared for him greatly.

sentences.zh: 今荊南定，吾東兵可無後患矣。」

translations.literal: Now Jingnan is settled; our eastern army can be without worry for the rear."
translations.idiomatic: Now Jingnan is secure; the eastern army has no rear to fear."

sentences.zh: 乃親作手詔褒之，命右丞廉希憲守江陵，促阿里海牙急還鄂，且以沿江諸城新附者委之。

translations.literal: He personally wrote a hand-edict to praise him, ordered Right Vice Administrator Lian Xixian to hold Jiangling, urged Ariq Qaya to hurry back to E, and moreover entrusted to him the newly submitted cities along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai wrote a personal edict of praise, left Lian Xixian at Jiangling, summoned Ariq Qaya back to E, and entrusted him with the newly submitted river cities.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙至鄂，招潭州守臣李芾，不聽。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya reached E and summoned Tanzhou's defending minister Li Fei; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Ezhou, Ariq Qaya summoned Tanzhou's defender Li Fei; he refused.

sentences.zh: 乃移兵長沙，拔湘陰。

translations.literal: He then moved troops to Changsha and took Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He shifted to Changsha and took Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，至潭，為書射城中以示芾，曰：「速下，以活州民，否則屠矣。」

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he reached Tan; writing a letter he shot it into the city to show Fei, saying: "Surrender quickly to save the prefecture's people; otherwise they will be slaughtered."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he reached Tanzhou, shot a letter into the city telling Fei, "Surrender now to save your people—or face slaughter."

sentences.zh: 不答。

translations.literal: There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fei did not answer.

sentences.zh: 乃決隍水，部分諸將，以砲攻之，破其木堡。

translations.literal: He then breached the moat water, divided sections among the generals, and with cannon attacked, breaking their wooden fort.
translations.idiomatic: He breached the moat, divided his generals, and bombarded the wooden fort until it broke.

sentences.zh: 流矢中胸，瘡甚，督戰益急，奪其城。

translations.literal: A stray arrow struck his chest; the wound was severe; supervising battle he became still more urgent, seized the city.
translations.idiomatic: A stray arrow pierced his chest; though badly wounded he pressed the assault harder and took the city.

sentences.zh: 潭人復作月城以相拒。

translations.literal: The people of Tan again built a crescent wall to resist each other.
translations.idiomatic: The Tanzhou people threw up an outer crescent wall to keep fighting.

sentences.zh: 凡攻七十日，大小數十戰。

translations.literal: In all they attacked seventy days; large and small battles numbered several tens.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted seventy days with dozens of major and minor battles.

sentences.zh: 十有三年春正月，芾力屈，及轉運使鐘蜚英、都統陳義皆自殺，其將劉孝忠以城降。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring of the thirteenth year Fei's strength was exhausted; Transport Commissioner Zhong Feiying and Regimental Commander Chen Yi all killed themselves; his general Liu Xiaozhong surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the thirteenth year Fei broke; Transport Commissioner Zhong Feiying and Regimental Commander Chen Yi killed themselves; General Liu Xiaozhong surrendered.

sentences.zh: 諸將欲屠之，阿里海牙曰：「是州生齒數百萬口，若悉殺之，非上諭伯顏以曹彬不殺意也，其屈法生之。」

translations.literal: The generals wished to slaughter the city; Ariq Qaya said: "This prefecture has several million living mouths; if all are killed, that is not the meaning of the sovereign's instruction to Bayan in the manner of Cao Bin's not killing; bend the law and let them live."
translations.idiomatic: The generals wanted a massacre; Ariq Qaya said, "This city holds millions; slaughter them all and we betray the Emperor's order to Bayan to follow Cao Bin's example of mercy—spare them even if we must bend the law."

sentences.zh: 復發倉以食饑者。

translations.literal: He again opened granaries to feed the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: He opened granaries to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 遣使徇郴、全、道、桂陽、永、衡、武岡、寶慶、袁、韶、南雄諸郡，其守臣皆率其民來迎，曰：「聞丞相體皇帝好生之德，毋殺虜，所過皆秋毫無犯，民今復見太平，各奉表來降。」

translations.literal: He sent envoys to march on Chen, Quan, Dao, Guiyang, Yong, Heng, Wugang, Baoqing, Yuan, Shao, Nanxiong, and other commanderies; their defending ministers all led their people to welcome him, saying: "We heard the Chancellor embodies the Emperor's virtue of cherishing life, does not kill captives, and wherever he passes not even a hair is harmed—the people now again see peace; each presents a memorial to surrender."
translations.idiomatic: Envoys marched on Chen, Quan, Dao, Guiyang, Yong, Heng, Wugang, Baoqing, Yuan, Shao, Nanxiong, and others; every defender came out with his people saying, "We hear the Chancellor honors the Emperor's mercy, takes no captives for slaughter, and harms nothing on his march—we see peace again and submit."

sentences.zh: 丞相，稱阿里海牙也。

translations.literal: Chancellor—this referred to Ariq Qaya.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor" meant Ariq Qaya.

sentences.zh: 奏官其降官，皆如江陵。

translations.literal: Memorializing, he appointed officials for those who surrendered—all as at Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: He reported surrendered officials for appointment, as at Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 獨宋經略使馬既守靜江不下。

translations.literal: Only Song Frontier Commissioner Ma Ji held Jingjiang and would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: Only Song Frontier Commissioner Ma Ji still held Jingjiang and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 使總管俞全等招之，皆為所殺。

translations.literal: He sent Supervisor Yu Quan and others to summon him; all were killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Supervisor Yu Quan and others to summon Ji; Ji killed them all.

sentences.zh: 會宋主以國降，降手詔遣湘山僧宗勉諭既，既復殺之。

translations.literal: Just then the Song ruler surrendered the state; a surrender hand-edict sent the Xiangshan monk Zongmian to instruct Ji; Ji again killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song emperor surrendered the realm, a hand-edict sent the monk Zongmian of Xiangshan to instruct Ji; Ji killed him too.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙又為書，以天命地利人心開既，許以廣西大都督，反覆千餘言，終不聽。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya again wrote a letter, opening Ji with Heaven's mandate, terrain, and popular will, promising him Grand Commander of Guangxi; repeatedly more than a thousand words— in the end he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya wrote again at length—more than a thousand words—appealing to mandate, terrain, and hearts, offering Grand Commander of Guangxi; Ji still refused.

sentences.zh: 因入朝賀平宋，拜平章政事，使持詔如靜江諭之。

translations.literal: He then entered court to congratulate the pacification of Song, was appointed Grand Councillor of State, and was sent holding an edict to Jingjiang to instruct Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court to celebrate the conquest of Song, was made Grand Councillor, and was sent with an edict to instruct Ji at Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，前兵至嚴關，既守關弗納，破其兵，又敗都統馬應麒於小溶江，遂逼靜江。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the vanguard reached Yan Pass; Ji guarded the pass and would not admit them; they broke his troops and again defeated Regimental Commander Ma Yingqi at Xiaorong River, then pressed Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the vanguard reached Yan Pass; Ji blocked it; they broke his force, defeated Regimental Commander Ma Yingqi at Xiaorong River, and closed on Jingjiang.

sentences.zh: 錄上所賜靜江詔以示既，既焚之，斬其使。

translations.literal: Recording the edict bestowed by the sovereign for Jingjiang, he showed it to Ji; Ji burned it and beheaded the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: They displayed the imperial edict for Jingjiang; Ji burned it and beheaded the bearer.

sentences.zh: 靜江以水為固，乃築堰斷大陽、小溶二江，以遏上流，決東南埭，以涸其隍，破其城。

translations.literal: Jingjiang relied on water as its strength; they then built dikes to cut the Dayang and Xiaorong rivers to check the upper reaches, breached the southeast embankment to drain its moat, and broke the city.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjiang's strength was water; they dammed the Dayang and Xiaorong to choke the upper streams, breached the southeast dike to drain the moat, and stormed the city.

sentences.zh: 民聞城破，即縱火焚居室，多赴水死。

translations.literal: When the people heard the city was broken, they immediately set fires to burn their dwellings; many rushed into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell the people torched their homes; many drowned themselves.

sentences.zh: 既及其總制黃文政、總管張虎以殘兵突圍走，執之。

translations.literal: Ji together with his Controller-in-Chief Huang Wenzheng and Supervisor Zhang Hu broke out with remnant troops and fled; they were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Ji broke out with Controller Huang Wenzheng and Supervisor Zhang Hu; all were captured.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙以靜江民易叛，非潭比，不重刑之，則廣西諸州不服，因悉坑之，斬既於市。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya, because the people of Jingjiang were easily rebellious—not comparable to Tan—if heavy punishment was not applied, then the commanderies of Guangxi would not submit; accordingly he buried them all in pits and executed Ji in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya judged Jingjiang's people more rebellious than Tanzhou's; without harsh example Guangxi would not submit—he had them buried alive in pits and executed Ji in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 分遣萬戶脫溫不花徇賓、融、柳、欽、橫、邕、慶遠，齊榮祖徇郁林、貴、廉、象，脫鄰徇潯、容、藤、梧，皆下之。

translations.literal: Separately he sent Ten-Thousand-Household Totoqbuqa to march on Bin, Rong, Liu, Qin, Heng, Yong, and Qingyuan; Qi Rongzu to march on Yulin, Gui, Lian, and Xiang; Tolin to march on Xun, Rong, Teng, and Wu—all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ten-Thousand-Household Totoqbuqa against Bin, Rong, Liu, Qin, Heng, Yong, and Qingyuan; Qi Rongzu against Yulin, Gui, Lian, and Xiang; Tolin against Xun, Rong, Teng, and Wu—all fell.

sentences.zh: 特磨王儂士貴、南丹州牧莫大秀，皆奉表求內附，奏官其降官如潭州。

translations.literal: Temmo King Nong Shigui and Nandan Prefecture Shepherd Mo Daxiu both presented memorials requesting inner submission; memorializing, he appointed officials for those who surrendered as at Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Temmo King Nong Shigui and Nandan Prefect Mo Daxiu both petitioned to submit; he reported their officials for appointment as at Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 以兵戍靜江、昭、賀、梧、邕、融，乃還潭。

translations.literal: With troops he garrisoned Jingjiang, Zhao, He, Wu, Yong, and Rong, then returned to Tan.
translations.idiomatic: He garrisoned Jingjiang, Zhao, He, Wu, Yong, and Rong, then returned to Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 既而宋二王稱制海中，雷、瓊、全、永與潭屬縣之民文才喻、周隆、張虎、羅飛咸起兵應之，舒、黃、蘄相繼亦起，大者眾數萬，小者不下數千。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the two Song princes proclaimed regency on the sea; Lei, Qiong, Quan, Yong, and the counties subordinate to Tan—Wen Caiyu, Zhou Long, Zhang Hu, Luo Fei—all raised troops in response; Shu, Huang, and Qi successively also rose—large ones had multitudes of tens of thousands, small ones no fewer than several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the two Song princes held court at sea; Wen Caiyu, Zhou Long, Zhang Hu, and Luo Fei raised the counties of Lei, Qiong, Quan, Yong, and Tan's dependencies; Shu, Huang, and Qi rebelled too—some with tens of thousands, none with fewer than thousands.

sentences.zh: 詔命討之，且略地海外。

translations.literal: An edict ordered them punished and moreover to seize territory overseas.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts ordered suppression and extension overseas.

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙既定才喻等，至雷州，使人諭瓊州安撫趙與珞降，不聽。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya, having settled Caiyu and the others, reached Lei Prefecture; he sent men to instruct Qiongzhou Pacification Commissioner Zhao Yuluo to surrender; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: After crushing Caiyu and the rest, Ariq Qaya reached Lei Prefecture and summoned Qiongzhou Pacification Commissioner Zhao Yuluo; he refused.

sentences.zh: 遂自航大海五百里，執與珞、冉安國、黃之紀，皆裂殺之，盡定瓊南寧、萬安、吉陽地。

translations.literal: He then himself sailed the great sea five hundred li, seized Yuluo, Ran Anguo, and Huang Zhiji, all dismembered and killed; he fully settled the lands of Qiongnan, Ning, Wan'an, and Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed five hundred li across the sea himself, seized Yuluo, Ran Anguo, and Huang Zhiji and had them dismembered, and pacified Qiongnan, Ning, Wan'an, and Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 降八蕃羅甸蠻，以其總管龍文貌入見，置宣慰司。

translations.literal: The Eight Fan Luo Dian barbarians submitted; their supervisor Long Wenmao entered audience; a Pacification Commission was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Eight Fan Luo Dian tribes submitted; their supervisor Long Wenmao came to court; a Pacification Commission was set up.

sentences.zh: 八蕃羅甸、臥龍、羅蕃、大龍、退蠻、盧蕃、小龍、石蕃、方蕃、洪蕃、程蕃，並置安撫以鎮之。

translations.literal: Eight Fan Luo Dian, Wolong, Luofan, Dalong, Tuiman, Lufan, Xiaolong, Shifan, Fangfan, Hongfan, and Chengfan—all had Pacification Commissioners established to garrison them.
translations.idiomatic: Eight Fan Luo Dian, Wolong, Luofan, Dalong, Tuiman, Lufan, Xiaolong, Shifan, Fangfan, Hongfan, and Chengfan each received pacification offices.

sentences.zh: 十八年，奏請徙省鄂州。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he memorialized requesting to move the Secretariat to E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he petitioned to move the secretariat to E Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 所定荊南、淮西、江西、海南、廣西之地，凡得州五十八，峒夷山獠不可勝計。

translations.literal: The lands settled in Jingnan, Huaidong West, Jiangxi, Hainan, and Guangxi—in all he obtained fifty-eight prefectures; cave barbarians and mountain liao were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingnan, Huaidong West, Jiangxi, Hainan, and Guangxi he secured fifty-eight prefectures and countless cave tribes and mountain liao.

sentences.zh: 大率以口舌降之，未嘗專事殺戮。

translations.literal: For the most part he brought them down by words and tongue; he never specialized in killing.
translations.idiomatic: He relied mostly on persuasion, not slaughter.

sentences.zh: 又其取民悉定從輕賦，民所在立祠祀之。

translations.literal: Moreover in taking from the people he wholly fixed light levies; wherever the people were, they established shrines to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: He kept levies light; wherever he ruled the people built shrines to him.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，入朝，加光祿大夫、湖廣行省左丞相；

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he entered court and was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Left Chancellor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he came to court and was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Left Chancellor of the Huguang Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十。

translations.literal: he died at age sixty.
translations.idiomatic: he died at sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司、上柱國，封楚國公，謚武定。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Preceptor with the same rites as the Three Excellencies and Grand Preceptor of State; enfeoffed as Duke of Chu with posthumous title Wuding.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor with rites equal to the Three Excellencies and as Grand Preceptor of State; enfeoffed Duke of Chu with posthumous title Wuding.

sentences.zh: 至正八年，進封江陵王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhizheng he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizheng 8 he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 子忽失海牙，湖廣行中書省左丞；

translations.literal: His son Qoshqai was Left Vice Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: His son Qoshqai was Left Vice Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat;

sentences.zh: 貫只哥，江西行中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: Gunjek was Grand Councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Gunjek was Grand Councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: ○相威

translations.literal: ○ Xiangwei
translations.idiomatic: ○ Xiangwei

sentences.zh: 相威，國王速渾察之子也。

translations.literal: Xiangwei was the son of King Suqunqa.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangwei was the son of King Suqunqa.

sentences.zh: 性弘毅重厚，不飲酒，寡言笑。

translations.literal: By nature he was magnanimous, resolute, and grave; he did not drink wine and spoke and laughed little.
translations.idiomatic: He was magnanimous, resolute, and sober-minded; he drank little and spoke sparingly.

sentences.zh: 喜延士大夫，聽讀經史，諭古今治亂，至直臣盡忠、良將制勝，必為之擊節稱善。

translations.literal: He delighted in receiving scholar-officials, listening to the reading of classics and histories, and instructing on the ordering and disorder of ancient and modern times; whenever he reached upright ministers giving full loyalty or good generals achieving victory, he always beat the measure and praised what was good.
translations.idiomatic: He welcomed scholars, listened to the classics and histories, and discussed governance past and present; at tales of loyal ministers or victorious generals he always clapped and praised.

sentences.zh: 以故臨大事，決大議，言必中節。

translations.literal: For this reason, when facing great affairs and deciding great deliberations, his words always hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in great affairs and weighty decisions his counsel always struck true.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，世祖命相威總速渾察元統弘吉剌等五投下兵從伐宋。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan the Founder ordered Xiangwei to command the troops of Suqunqa's original banner and the five appanage banners of Hongjila and others to follow in attacking Song.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 11 Kublai ordered Xiangwei to lead Suqunqa's original banner and five Hongjila appanage contingents against Song.

sentences.zh: 由正陽取安豐，略廬，克和，攻司空山，平野人原。

translations.literal: From Zhengyang he took Anfeng, raided Lu, captured He, attacked Sikong Mountain, and pacified the Wild People's Plain.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhengyang he took Anfeng, raided Lu, captured He, stormed Sikong Mountain, and pacified the Wild People's Plain.

sentences.zh: 道安慶，渡江東下，會丞相伯顏兵於潤州，分三道並進，相威率左軍，參政董文炳為副，部署將校，申明約束。

translations.literal: Passing Anqing, he crossed the river and went downstream, joined Chancellor Bayan's army at Runzhou, divided into three routes and advanced together; Xiangwei led the left army, Vice Administrator Dong Wenbing as deputy, deploying generals and officers and clarifying regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed at Anqing, sailed downriver, joined Bayan at Runzhou, and advanced in three columns—Xiangwei leading the left with Vice Administrator Dong Wenbing as deputy, assigning commands and enforcing discipline.

sentences.zh: 江陰、華亭、澉浦、上海悉望風款附，吏民按堵如故。

translations.literal: Jiangyin, Huating, Ganpu, and Shanghai all submitted on sight of his banners; officials and people remained settled as before.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangyin, Huating, Ganpu, and Shanghai submitted at his approach; civil order was undisturbed.

sentences.zh: 進屯鹽官，伯顏已駐師臨安城下，得宋幼主降表。

translations.literal: Advancing he garrisoned at Yanguan; Bayan had already stationed his army below Lin'an city and obtained the Song young ruler's surrender memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Yanguan while Bayan already held Lin'an and received the young Song emperor's surrender.

sentences.zh: 相威乃移兵瓜洲，與阿術兵合。

translations.literal: Xiangwei then moved troops to Guazhou and joined Aju's army.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangwei then shifted to Guazhou and united with Aju.

sentences.zh: 臨揚州，都統姜才以兵二萬攻揚子橋，率諸將擊敗之。

translations.literal: Approaching Yangzhou, Regimental Commander Jiang Cai with twenty thousand troops attacked Yangzi Bridge; leading the generals he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Near Yangzhou, Regimental Commander Jiang Cai attacked Yangzi Bridge with twenty thousand men; Xiangwei led the generals and routed him.

sentences.zh: 十三年夏，驛召相威。

translations.literal: In the summer of the thirteenth year he was summoned by post horse.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the thirteenth year he was summoned by courier.

sentences.zh: 秋，入覲，大饗，賚功，授金虎符、征西都元帥，仍賜弓矢甲鞍、文錦表裡四、鈔萬貫，從者賞賜有差。

translations.literal: In autumn he entered audience; a great feast was held and merit rewarded; he was appointed Marshal of the West Expedition with a gold tiger tally, and still granted bow, arrows, armor, saddle, four brocade outer and inner garments, ten thousand strings of paper money, and followers rewarded in differing degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn he appeared at court; after a great feast he received the gold tiger tally as Marshal of the Western Expedition, plus bow, arrows, armor, saddle, brocade garments, ten thousand strings of paper money, and graded rewards for his followers.

sentences.zh: 時親王海都叛，命領汪總帥兵以鎮西土。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Haidu rebelled; he was ordered to lead Commander Wang's troops to garrison the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Haidu rebelled he was ordered to lead Commander Wang's force to secure the west.

sentences.zh: 十四年，召拜江南諸道行台御史大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was summoned and appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was recalled as Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.

sentences.zh: 乃上奏曰：「陛下以臣為耳目，臣以監察御史、按察司為耳目。

translations.literal: He then memorialized upward: "Your Majesty takes me as eyes and ears; I take surveillance censors and the intendant offices as eyes and ears.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Your Majesty makes me your eyes and ears; I make the surveillance censors and intendant offices mine.

sentences.zh: 倘非其人，是人之耳目先自閉塞，下情何由上達。」

translations.literal: If they are not the right men, then people's eyes and ears are first blocked themselves—how can lower feelings reach upward?"
translations.idiomatic: If those men are unworthy, the people's eyes and ears are stopped first—how can grievances reach the throne?"

sentences.zh: 帝嘉之，命御史臺清其選。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended this and ordered the Censorate to purify its selections.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised this and ordered the Censorate to clean up its appointments.

sentences.zh: 每除目至，必集幕僚御史議其可否，不協公論者即劾去之。

translations.literal: Whenever appointment notices arrived, he always gathered staff censors to discuss whether they were acceptable; those not matching public opinion he immediately impeached and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever appointments arrived he convened his censors to debate them and impeached anyone the consensus rejected.

sentences.zh: 繼陳便民一十五事，其略曰：並行省，削冗官，鈐鎮戍，拘官船，業流民，錄故官，贓饋遺，淮浙鹽運司直隸行省，行大司農營田司並入宣慰司，理訟勿分南北，公田召佃仍減其租，革宋公吏勿容作弊。

translations.literal: Subsequently he presented fifteen matters for the people's convenience; the outline said: merge branch secretariats, cut redundant officials, tighten garrison control, restrict official ships, settle displaced people, record former officials, punish bribery gifts, make the Huai-Zhe Salt Transport Office directly subordinate to the branch secretariat, merge the Grand Agriculture and Colonization offices into the Pacification Commission, adjudicate lawsuits without dividing north and south, summon tenants for public fields while still reducing rent, reform Song clerks and do not tolerate fraud.
translations.idiomatic: He then offered fifteen reforms: merge branch secretariats, cut redundant posts, tighten garrisons, restrict official shipping, resettle refugees, register former officials, punish bribery, place the Huai-Zhe salt office under the branch secretariat, fold the agriculture and colonization offices into the pacification commission, try cases without north-south division, lease public fields at reduced rent, and curb Song clerical abuses.

sentences.zh: 帝皆納焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor all accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted them all.

sentences.zh: 浙東盜起，浙西宣慰使昔裡伯縱兵肆掠，俘及平民，乃遣御史商琥據錢唐津渡閱治之，得釋者以數千計。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in eastern Zhe; the Zhexi Pacification Commissioner Shili Bo let troops plunder at will, capturing even civilians; he sent Censor Shang Huo to inspect at the Qiantang ferry crossing and obtained releases numbering in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in eastern Zhe; Zhexi Pacification Commissioner Shili Bo's men looted civilians; Xiangwei sent Censor Shang Huo to investigate at the Qiantang crossing and freed thousands.

sentences.zh: 昔裡伯遁還都，奏執還揚州治其罪。

translations.literal: Shili Bo fled back to the capital and memorialized to have him seized and returned to Yangzhou to punish his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Shili Bo fled to the capital and petitioned to have Shang Huo arrested and sent back to Yangzhou for trial.

sentences.zh: 十六年，入覲，會左丞崔斌等言平章阿合馬不法事，有旨命相威及知樞密院博羅自開平馳驛大都共鞫之。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he entered audience; just then Left Vice Administrator Cui Bin and others spoke of Associate Grand Councillor Ahmad's unlawful conduct; there was an order for Xiangwei and Military Affairs Commissioner Boluo to ride post horses from Kaiping to Dadu together to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he came to court as Left Vice Administrator Cui Bin and others accused Associate Grand Councillor Ahmad of corruption; Kublai ordered Xiangwei and Military Affairs Commissioner Boluo to ride post from Kaiping to Dadu to investigate.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬稱疾不出，博羅欲回，相威厲聲色曰：「奉旨按問，敢回奏耶！」

translations.literal: Ahmad claimed illness and would not appear; Boluo wished to turn back; Xiangwei in stern voice said: "We have orders to investigate—dare we return and memorialize!"
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad feigned illness; Boluo wanted to withdraw; Xiangwei said sharply, "We are ordered to investigate—shall we go back empty-handed?"

sentences.zh: 令輿疾赴對，首責數事。

translations.literal: He ordered him carried sick to answer; first he charged several matters.
translations.idiomatic: He had Ahmad brought sick to answer and charged him on several counts first.

sentences.zh: 既引伏，有旨釋免，仍喻相威曰：「朕知卿不惜顏面。」

translations.literal: Having confessed, there was an order to release and pardon; still instructing Xiangwei: "I know you do not spare your face."
translations.idiomatic: After Ahmad confessed, an order pardoned him; Kublai told Xiangwei, "I know you do not spare your own face for mine."

sentences.zh: 復命還南行台。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to return to the southern branch censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent back to the southern censorate.

sentences.zh: 十七年，有旨命相威檢核阿里海牙、忽都帖木兒等所俘三萬二千餘口，並放為民。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year there was an order for Xiangwei to inspect and verify the more than thirty-two thousand captives taken by Ariq Qaya, Hudutemür, and others, and release them all as civilians.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was ordered to audit more than thirty-two thousand captives taken by Ariq Qaya, Hudutemür, and others and free them as civilians.

sentences.zh: 十八年，右丞範文虎、參政李庭以兵十萬航海徵倭。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Right Vice Administrator Fan Wenhu and Vice Administrator Li Ting with a hundred thousand troops went by sea to campaign against Japan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Right Vice Administrator Fan Wenhu and Vice Administrator Li Ting sailed with a hundred thousand men against Japan.

sentences.zh: 七晝夜至竹島，與遼陽省臣兵合。

translations.literal: In seven days and nights they reached Zhudao and joined the Liaoyang provincial troops.
translations.idiomatic: In seven days and nights they reached Zhudao and joined the Liaoyang provincial force.

sentences.zh: 欲先攻太宰府，遲疑不發。

translations.literal: They wished first to attack the Dazaifu but hesitated and did not launch.
translations.idiomatic: They meant to strike Dazaifu first but hesitated and did not attack.

sentences.zh: 八月朔，颶風大作，士卒十喪六七。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month a great hurricane arose; six or seven of ten soldiers perished.
translations.idiomatic: On the first of the eighth month a typhoon struck; six or seven in ten soldiers perished.

sentences.zh: 帝震怒，復命行省左丞相阿塔海征之。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly enraged and again ordered Branch Secretariat Left Chancellor Atahai to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai was furious and ordered Branch Left Chancellor Atahai to invade again.

sentences.zh: 一時無敢諫者。

translations.literal: For a time none dared remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: For a time no one dared object.

sentences.zh: 相威遣使入奏曰：「倭不奉職貢，可伐而不可恕，可緩而不可急。

translations.literal: Xiangwei sent an envoy to memorialize upward: "Japan does not offer tribute and service—it may be punished but should not be pardoned; it may be delayed but should not be rushed.
