translations.idiomatic: Xiangwei sent a memorial: "Japan withholds tribute—it may be punished but not indulged; the campaign may wait but must not be rushed.

sentences.zh: 向者師行迫期，戰船不堅，前車已覆，後當改轍。

translations.literal: Previously the army marched pressing the deadline; war ships were not staunch; the cart ahead already overturned—the rear should change the track.
translations.idiomatic: The last expedition was forced by deadline with unseaworthy ships; the cart ahead already overturned—the rear must change course.

sentences.zh: 今為之計，預修戰艦，訓練士卒，耀兵揚武，使彼聞之，深自備禦。

translations.literal: Now for planning: beforehand repair war ships, train soldiers, display troops and raise martial renown, so that when they hear of it they deeply prepare defenses themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The plan now: build warships, drill troops, show force so they hear and arm themselves heavily.

sentences.zh: 遲以歲月，俟其疲怠，出其不意，乘風疾往，一舉而下，萬全之策也。」

translations.literal: Delay months and years; wait until they are weary and slack; go out where they do not expect, ride the wind swiftly—one stroke and it falls; this is the strategy of complete security."
translations.idiomatic: Wait months and years until they tire; then strike where they do not expect, ride the wind, and take them in one blow—that is the safe course."

sentences.zh: 帝意始釋，遂罷其役。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind was then released; the expedition was thereupon halted.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor relented and halted the expedition.

sentences.zh: 又陳皇太子既令中書，宜領撫軍監國之任，選正人端士，立詹事、賓客、諭德、贊善，衛翼左右，所以樹國本也。

translations.literal: He again presented that since the Crown Prince had already ordered the Central Secretariat, he ought to bear the duties of comforting the army and overseeing the state; select upright men and fine scholars, establish Grand Mentors, Guests, Preceptors, and Supporters to flank and assist left and right—this is how to plant the root of the state.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged that with the Crown Prince already directing the Secretariat, he should oversee the realm and the army; appoint upright scholars as Grand Mentor, Guest, Preceptor, and Supporter to guard him—that is how to secure the succession.

sentences.zh: 帝深然之。

translations.literal: The Emperor deeply approved.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 十九年，又奏阿里海牙占降民一千八百戶為奴，阿里海牙以為征討所得，有旨：「果降民也，還之有司；

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he again memorialized that Ariq Qaya occupied one thousand eight hundred households of submitted people as slaves; Ariq Qaya considered them obtained by campaigning;
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he reported that Ariq Qaya had enslaved eighteen hundred submitted households; Ariq Qaya claimed them as campaign spoils;

sentences.zh: 若征討所得，令御史臺籍其數以聞，量賜有功者。」

translations.literal: there was an order: "If they are truly submitted people, return them to the offices; if obtained by campaigning, let the Censorate register the numbers and report, and measure gifts to those with merit."
translations.idiomatic: the order came: "If they are submitted people, return them to the offices; if spoils of war, let the Censorate register and reward merit accordingly."

sentences.zh: 阿里海牙又自陳其功比伯顏，當賜養老戶，御史滕魯瞻劾之，阿里海牙自辨，有旨遣使赴行台逮問。

translations.literal: Ariq Qaya again himself presented that his merit compared with Bayan's and he ought to be granted old-age households; Censor Teng Luzhan impeached him; Ariq Qaya defended himself; there was an order to send an envoy to the branch censorate to seize and question.
translations.idiomatic: Ariq Qaya claimed merit equal to Bayan's and demanded retirement households; Censor Teng Luzhan impeached him; an envoy was sent to the branch censorate to arrest and question him.

sentences.zh: 相威曰：「為臣敢爾欺誑邪，滕御史何罪。」

translations.literal: Xiangwei said: "As a minister dare he thus deceive! What crime has Censor Teng?"
translations.idiomatic: Xiangwei said, "Would a minister dare such fraud? What crime has Censor Teng committed?"

sentences.zh: 即馳奏，使者竟歸。

translations.literal: He immediately memorialized by post horse; the envoy in the end returned.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized by urgent courier; the envoy was recalled.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以疾請入覲，進譯語《資治通鑒》，帝即以賜東宮經筵講讀。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, ill, he requested to enter audience; he presented a translated Zizhi Tongjian; the Emperor immediately bestowed it on the Eastern Palace for lecture and reading.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, ill, he asked to come to court and presented a translated Zizhi Tongjian; Kublai gave it to the Eastern Palace for study.

sentences.zh: 拜江淮行省左丞相。

translations.literal: He was appointed Left Chancellor of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Chancellor of the Jianghuai Branch Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，啟行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he took up the post.

sentences.zh: 四月，卒於蠡州，年四十四。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he died at Li Prefecture at age forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he died at Li Prefecture, aged forty-four.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，帝悼惜不已。

translations.literal: When the obituary was heard, the Emperor mourned and regretted without end.
translations.idiomatic: News of his death brought Kublai's lasting grief.

sentences.zh: 子阿老瓦丁，南行台御史大夫；

translations.literal: His son Alawading was Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Branch Censorate;
translations.idiomatic: His son Alawading became Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Branch Censorate;

sentences.zh: 孫脫歡，集賢大學士。

translations.literal: his grandson Toghan was Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: his grandson Toghan was Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: ○土土哈

translations.literal: ○ Tutuha
translations.idiomatic: ○ Tutuha

sentences.zh: 土土哈，其先本武平北折連川按答罕山部族，自曲出徙居西北玉裡伯裡山，因以為氏，號其國曰欽察。

translations.literal: Tutuha—his ancestors originally were of the tribe at Mount Andaqan of Beizhelianchuan in Wuping; from Ququ they moved to dwell at Mount Yiliboli in the northwest and took it as their surname; they styled their state Qipchaq.
translations.idiomatic: Tutuha's ancestors were of the Beizhelianchuan Andaqan tribe in Wuping; moving from Ququ to Mount Yiliboli in the northwest, they took that name and styled their realm Qipchaq.

sentences.zh: 其地去中國三萬餘里，夏夜極短，日暫沒即出。

translations.literal: That land was more than thirty thousand li from China; in summer nights it was extremely short—the sun briefly set and then came out.
translations.idiomatic: Their land lay more than thirty thousand li from China; summer nights were so short the sun barely dipped below the horizon before rising again.

sentences.zh: 曲出生唆末納，唆末納生亦納思，世為欽察國王。

translations.literal: Ququ begot Somina; Somina begot Inas; for generations they were kings of Qipchaq.
translations.idiomatic: Ququ begot Somina; Somina begot Inas; for generations they ruled Qipchaq.

sentences.zh: 太祖徵蔑裡乞，其主火都奔欽察，亦納思納之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor campaigned against Merkit; its lord Hudu fled to Qipchaq and Inas received him.
translations.idiomatic: When Genghis Khan campaigned against the Merkits, their lord Hudu fled to Qipchaq and Inas sheltered him.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣使諭之曰：「汝奚匿吾負箭之麋？

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor sent an envoy to instruct him: "Why do you hide my arrow-bearing elk?
translations.idiomatic: Genghis sent envoys demanding, "Why do you hide my quarry—the elk who bears my arrow?

sentences.zh: 亟以相還，不然禍且及汝。」

translations.literal: Quickly return him; otherwise disaster will reach you."
translations.idiomatic: Return him at once or disaster will find you."

sentences.zh: 亦納思答曰：「逃鸇之雀，叢薄猶能生之，吾顧不如草木耶？」

translations.literal: Inas replied: "A sparrow fleeing the hawk—even thickets can give it life; am I not better than grass and trees?"
translations.idiomatic: Inas replied, "Even a sparrow fleeing the hawk finds shelter in the brush—am I less merciful than the grass?"

sentences.zh: 太祖乃命將討之。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor then ordered generals to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis then sent armies against them.

sentences.zh: 亦納思已老，國中大亂，亦納思之子忽魯速蠻遣使自歸於太宗。

translations.literal: Inas was already old; inside the state there was great disorder; Inas's son Qulussun sent envoys to submit to himself to Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Inas was aged and his realm in turmoil; his son Qulussun sent envoys submitting to Ögedei.

sentences.zh: 而憲宗受命帥師，已扣其境，忽魯速蠻之子班都察舉族迎降。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong received command as commander-in-chief, he had already knocked at their borders; Qulussun's son Banducha led the whole clan to welcome and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke took supreme command he already pressed their frontier; Qulussun's son Banducha led the clan in submission.

sentences.zh: 從徵麥怯斯有功。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Merv he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Merv campaign with distinction.

sentences.zh: 率欽察百人從世祖徵大理，伐宋，以強勇稱。

translations.literal: Leading a hundred Qipchaqs he followed the Founder in campaigning against Dali and attacking Song, renowned for strength and courage.
translations.idiomatic: Leading a hundred Qipchaqs he followed Kublai against Dali and Song, famed for valor.

sentences.zh: 嘗侍左右，掌尚方馬畜，歲時挏馬乳以進，色清而味美，號黑馬乳，因目其屬曰哈剌赤。

translations.literal: He once attended at the side, managing the imperial stable's horses and livestock; at year's seasons he milked mares to present—clear in color and fine in taste—styled black mare's milk; accordingly he styled his followers Qaračin.
translations.idiomatic: He attended the Founder, overseeing imperial herds; each season he sent mare's milk—clear and fine—called black kumiss, and his household became known as the Qaračin.

sentences.zh: 宗王海都構亂，世祖以國家根本之地，命皇太子北平王率諸王鎮守之。

translations.literal: Prince Haidu plotted disorder; the Founder, because it was the land of the state's root and foundation, ordered the Crown Prince, the Prince of Beiping, to lead the princes to garrison and hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Haidu rebelled, Kublai—knowing the north was the dynasty's root—ordered the Crown Prince of Beiping and the princes to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，諸王脫脫木、失烈吉叛，寇抄諸部，掠祖宗所御大帳以去。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan, Princes Totoqmu and Shiregi rebelled, raided the various tribes, and carried off the great tent used by the ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 14 Princes Totoqmu and Shiregi rebelled, raided the tribes, and stole the ancestral great tent.

sentences.zh: 土土哈率兵討之，敗其將脫兒赤顏於納蘭不剌，邀諸部以還。

translations.literal: Tutuha led troops to punish them, defeated their general Togril at Nalanbula, and intercepted the tribes to return.
translations.idiomatic: Tutuha marched against them, defeated Togril at Nalanbula, and recovered the tribes.

sentences.zh: 應昌部族只兒瓦台構亂，脫脫木引兵應之，中途遇土土哈，將戰，先獲其候騎數十，脫脫木乃引去，遂滅只兒瓦台。

translations.literal: The Yingchang tribe Jirghatai plotted disorder; Totoqmu led troops to respond; midway he met Tutuha; about to give battle, he first captured several tens of their scout horsemen; Totoqmu then withdrew, and Jirghatai was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Yingchang chieftain Jirghatai rebelled; Totoqmu marched to join him but met Tutuha, lost his scouts, and withdrew; Jirghatai was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 追脫脫木等至禿兀剌河，三宿而後返。

translations.literal: Pursuing Totoqmu and the others to the Togla River, after three nights' stay he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued Totoqmu to the Togla River, camped three nights, and returned.

sentences.zh: 尋復敗之於斡歡河，奪回所掠大帳，還諸部之眾於北平。

translations.literal: Soon he again defeated them at the Ogna River, recovered the plundered great tent, and returned the tribes' multitudes to Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he beat them again at the Ogna River, recovered the stolen great tent, and restored the tribes to Beiping.

sentences.zh: 十五年，大軍北征，詔率欽察驍騎千人以從。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year the great army campaigned north; an edict ordered him to lead a thousand Qipchaq crack horsemen to follow.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year the northern campaign was ordered; Tutuha led a thousand Qipchaq horse.

sentences.zh: 追失烈吉逾金山，擒扎忽台等以獻。

translations.literal: Pursuing Shiregi beyond the Altai, he captured Zaqutai and others and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Shiregi beyond the Altai he captured Zaqutai and others and presented them.

sentences.zh: 又敗寬折哥等，裹瘡力戰，獲羊馬輜重甚眾。

translations.literal: Again he defeated Kuanjge and others; wrapping wounds he fought with force and obtained sheep, horses, and baggage in great number.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Kuanjge and others too; fighting through wounds he seized vast herds and baggage.

sentences.zh: 還朝，帝召至榻前，親慰勞之，賜金銀酒器及銀百兩、金幣九、歲時預宴只孫冠服全、海東白鶻一，仍賜以奪回所掠大帳，而諭之曰：「祖宗武帳，非人臣所得御，以卿能歸之，故以授卿。」

translations.literal: Returning to court, the Emperor summoned him before the couch, personally comforted and rewarded him, granted gold and silver wine vessels and a hundred taels of silver, nine gold coins, yearly pre-banquet zisun robes complete, one eastern white gyrfalcon, still granted the recovered plundered great tent, and instructed him: "The ancestors' martial tent is not what subjects may use—for you could return it, it is therefore granted to you."
translations.idiomatic: At court Kublai summoned him to the couch, comforted him, gave gold and silver vessels, a hundred taels of silver, nine gold coins, full zisun banquet robes, an eastern white gyrfalcon, and returned the recovered great tent, saying, "The ancestral war tent is not for subjects—but you restored it, so it is yours."

sentences.zh: 嘗有旨：「欽察人為民及隸諸王者，皆別籍之以隸土土哈，戶給鈔二千貫，歲賜粟帛，選其材勇，以備禁衛。」

translations.literal: There had been an order: "Qipchaq people who are civilians and those subordinate to princes—all separately register them to belong to Tutuha; each household granted two thousand strings of paper money, yearly grain and cloth bestowed, select their talent and courage to prepare for the palace guard."
translations.idiomatic: An edict had registered all Qipchaq civilians and princely dependents under Tutuha—two thousand strings per household, yearly grain and cloth, and the bravest chosen for the guard.

sentences.zh: 十九年，授昭勇大將軍、同知太僕院事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was appointed General of Brilliant Courage and Associate Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became General of Brilliant Courage and Associate Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 二十年，改同知衛尉院事，兼領群牧司。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was changed to Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and concurrently supervised the Herd Office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he became Associate Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments and supervised the Herd Office.

sentences.zh: 請以所部哈剌赤屯田畿內，詔給霸州文安縣田四百頃，益以宋新附軍人八百，俾領其事。

translations.literal: He requested to have his Qaračin subordinates colonize fields within the capital region; an edict granted four hundred qing of fields in Wen'an County, Bazhou, increased by eight hundred newly submitted Song soldiers, to let him lead the affair.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to settle his Qaračin as colonists near the capital; the court granted four hundred qing in Wen'an, Bazhou, plus eight hundred newly submitted Song troops under his command.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，賜金虎符，並賜金貂、裘帽、玉帶各一，海東青鶻一，水磑壹區，近郊田二千畝，籍河東諸路蒙古軍子弟四千六百人隸其麾下。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was granted a gold tiger tally, and still granted one gold sable, fur cap, and jade belt each, one eastern gyrfalcon, one water mill, two thousand mu of fields near the capital, and four thousand six hundred Mongol army youths from the Hedong circuits registered under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he received a gold tiger tally, sable and jade regalia, a gyrfalcon, a water mill, two thousand mu near the capital, and forty-six hundred Mongol youths from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，拜鎮國上將軍、樞密院副使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed General for Pacifying the State and Vice Director of the Military Affairs Commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was made General for Pacifying the State and Vice Director of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，置欽察親軍衛，遂兼都指揮使，聽以宗族將吏備官屬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the Qipchaq Palace Guard was established; he then concurrently became Commander-in-Chief, permitted to use clan generals and officers to fill official posts.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year the Qipchaq Guard was established; he became its commander and staffed it with kinsmen and officers.

sentences.zh: 海都兵犯金山，詔與大將朵兒朵懷共御之。

translations.literal: Haidu's troops violated the Altai; an edict ordered him together with the great general Dordön to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Haidu struck the Altai, he and General Dordön were ordered to meet him.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，宗王乃顏叛，陰遣使來結也不幹、勝剌哈，為土土哈所執，盡得其情以聞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year Prince Nayan rebelled; secretly he sent envoys to join Yebugan and Senggge; Tutuha seized them and fully obtained their circumstances to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year Prince Nayan rebelled and secretly contacted Yebugan and Senggge; Tutuha seized the envoys and reported all.

sentences.zh: 勝剌哈設宴邀二大將，朵兒朵懷將往，土土哈以為事不可測，遂止，勝剌哈計不得行。

translations.literal: Senggge set a banquet to invite the two great generals; Dordön was about to go; Tutuha thought the matter could not be measured and stopped it; Senggge's plan could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Senggge invited the two generals to a feast; Dordön meant to go; Tutuha stopped him as too risky; Senggge's plot failed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，有旨令勝剌哈入朝，將由東道進，土土哈言於北安王曰：「彼分地在東，脫有不虞，是縱虎入山林也。」

translations.literal: Before long there was an order for Senggge to enter court; he was to advance by the eastern route; Tutuha spoke to the Prince of Beian: "His fief is in the east—if unexpectedly something happens, that is releasing a tiger into mountain forests."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Senggge was ordered to court by the eastern road; Tutuha told the Prince of Beian, "His domain is east—send him that way and we release a tiger into the hills."

sentences.zh: 乃命從西道進。

translations.literal: He then ordered him to advance by the western route.
translations.idiomatic: He was made to travel the western road instead.

sentences.zh: 既而有言也不幹叛者，眾欲先聞於朝，然後發兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward there were words that Yebugan had rebelled; the multitude wished first to report to court and then send troops.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that Yebugan had rebelled; others wanted to report first, then march.

sentences.zh: 土土哈曰：「兵貴神速，若彼果叛，我軍出其不意，可即圖之；

translations.literal: Tutuha said: "In warfare speed is precious—if he indeed rebels, our army going where he does not expect can immediately take him;
translations.idiomatic: Tutuha said, "War favors speed—if he truly rebels, strike before he expects it;

sentences.zh: 否則與約而還。」

translations.literal: if not, make a pact and return.
translations.idiomatic: if not, make terms and return."

sentences.zh: 即日啟行，疾驅七晝夜，渡禿兀剌河，戰於孛怯嶺，大敗之，也不幹僅以身免。

translations.literal: That very day he set out; in seven days and nights of hard riding he crossed the Togla River and fought at Leqie Ridge; he routed them greatly; Yebugan barely escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: That day he marched; in seven days and nights he crossed the Togla and routed Yebugan at Leqie Ridge; Yebugan barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 世祖時親征乃顏，聞之，遣使命土土哈收其餘黨，沿河而下。

translations.literal: The Founder at the time personally campaigned against Nayan; hearing this, he sent orders for Tutuha to gather the remnant faction, going downstream along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai, campaigning against Nayan in person, ordered Tutuha to mop up downstream along the river.

sentences.zh: 遇叛王也鐵哥軍萬騎，擊走之，獲馬甚眾，並擒叛王哈兒魯等，獻俘行在所，誅之。

translations.literal: Meeting rebel Prince Yitek's army of ten thousand horsemen, he struck and drove them off, obtained horses in great number, and also captured rebel princes Qarluq and others; presenting captives at the mobile court, they were executed.
translations.idiomatic: He met Prince Yitek's ten thousand horse, drove them off, took many horses, captured princes Qarluq and others, and executed them before the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 欽察、康裡之屬，自叛所來歸者，即以付土土哈，置哈剌魯萬戶府，欽察之散處安西諸王部下者，悉令統之。

translations.literal: Qipchaq and Kangli dependents who came from the rebel place to submit were immediately entrusted to Tutuha; the Qarluq Ten-Thousand-Household office was established; Qipchaqs scattered among the Anxi princes were all ordered unified under him.
translations.idiomatic: Qipchaq and Kangli clans returning from the rebels were placed under Tutuha; the Qarluq Ten-Thousand-Household was established; scattered Qipchaqs under western princes were consolidated under him.

sentences.zh: 時成宗以皇孫撫軍於北，詔以土土哈從。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Chengzong as imperial grandson pacified the army in the north; an edict ordered Tutuha to follow.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong as imperial grandson commanded the north, Tutuha was ordered to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 追乃顏餘黨於哈剌，誅叛王兀塔海，盡降其眾。

translations.literal: Pursuing Nayan's remnant faction at Qara, he executed rebel prince Utahai and fully reduced their multitudes.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing Nayan's remnants at Qara he executed Prince Utahai and accepted the surrender of all.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，諸王也只裡為叛王火魯哈孫所攻，遣使告急。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Prince Yeje'er was attacked by rebel prince Qorqasun; he sent envoys reporting urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year Prince Yeje'er was attacked by rebel Prince Qorqasun and sent urgent pleas.

sentences.zh: 復從皇孫移師援之，敗諸兀魯灰。

translations.literal: Again following the imperial grandson he shifted troops to rescue; defeated the various Ulughai.
translations.idiomatic: Tutuha shifted with the imperial grandson to relieve him and defeated the Ulughai.

sentences.zh: 還至哈剌溫山，夜渡貴烈河，敗叛王哈丹，盡得遼左諸部，置東路萬戶府。

translations.literal: Returning to Mount Qalawun, by night he crossed the Guile River, defeated rebel prince Qadan, fully obtained the eastern departments, and established the Eastern Route Ten-Thousand-Household office.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Qalawun he crossed the Guile by night, beat Prince Qadan, secured the eastern departments, and established the Eastern Route Ten-Thousand-Household.

sentences.zh: 世祖多其功，以也只裡女弟塔倫妻之。

translations.literal: The Founder praised his merit and gave him Prince Yeje'er's younger sister Talun as wife.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai rewarded him with Prince Yeje'er's sister Talun in marriage.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，從皇孫晉王徵海都。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he followed the imperial grandson, the Prince of Jin, in campaigning against Haidu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he followed the Prince of Jin against Haidu.

sentences.zh: 抵杭海嶺，敵先據險，諸軍失利，惟土土哈以其軍直前鏖戰，翼晉王而出。

translations.literal: Reaching Hangai Ridge, the enemy first held the defiles; the armies suffered loss; only Tutuha with his army went straight forward in fierce battle and flanked the Prince of Jin out.
translations.idiomatic: At Hangai Ridge the enemy held the heights; the army faltered; only Tutuha fought straight through and escorted the Prince of Jin out.

sentences.zh: 追騎大至，乃選精銳設伏以待之，寇不敢逼。

translations.literal: Pursuing horsemen came in great numbers; he then selected elite troops and set an ambush to await them; the raiders did not dare press close.
translations.idiomatic: When pursuers closed in he chose elite men, laid ambush, and the enemy dared not press.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，世祖巡幸北邊，召見慰諭之，曰：「昔太祖與其臣同患難者，飲班術河之水以記功。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the Founder inspected the northern frontier; summoning him he comforted and instructed him, saying: "In old times the Grand Ancestor with his ministers shared hardship; drinking the waters of the Banshi River to record merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Kublai toured the northern frontier, summoned Tutuha, and said, "Genghis and his companions shared hardship and drank the Banshi River to seal their deeds.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，何愧昔人，卿其勉之。」

translations.literal: Today's affair—what shame before the men of old; you must exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Today's fight is no disgrace to those men—press on."

sentences.zh: 還至京師，大宴群臣，復謂土土哈曰：「朔方人來，聞海都言：『杭海之役，使彼邊將皆如土土哈，吾屬安所置哉！』

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, at a great feast for the ministers he again told Tutuha: "Men from the north came; they heard Haidu say: 'At the Hangai battle, if all their frontier generals were like Tutuha, where would we be placed!'
translations.idiomatic: Back at court, feasting his ministers, Kublai told Tutuha, "Northerners report Haidu said, 'At Hangai, if every frontier general were like Tutuha, where would we stand?'

sentences.zh: 」論功行賞，帝欲先欽察之士。

translations.literal: Ranking merit and distributing rewards, the Emperor wished first to reward Qipchaq warriors."
translations.idiomatic: When rewards were apportioned, the Emperor meant to favor the Qipchaq first."

sentences.zh: 土土哈言：「慶賞之典，蒙古將吏宜先之。」

translations.literal: Tutuha said: "In the canon of celebration and reward, Mongol generals and officers ought to come first."
translations.idiomatic: Tutuha said, "By custom Mongol officers should come first."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「爾毋飾讓，蒙古人誠居汝右，力戰豈在汝右耶？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Do not make modest refusal—Mongols indeed stand to your right, but in fierce fighting are they indeed to your right?"
translations.idiomatic: Kublai said, "Do not demur—Mongols rank above you, but in the thick of battle who stands ahead?"

sentences.zh: 召諸將頒賞有差。

translations.literal: He summoned the generals and distributed rewards in differing degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned the generals and gave graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 初，世祖既取宋，命籍建康、廬、饒租戶千為哈剌赤戶，益以俘獲千七百戶賜土土哈，仍官一子，以督其賦。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Founder having taken Song, ordered registration of a thousand rent households of Jiankang, Lu, and Rao as Qaračin households, increased by one thousand seven hundred captured households granted to Tutuha; still one son was appointed to office to supervise their levies.
translations.idiomatic: After conquering Song, Kublai registered a thousand rent households from Jiankang, Lu, and Rao as Qaračin households, added seventeen hundred captives for Tutuha, and appointed a son to oversee the levies.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，土土哈奏：「哈剌赤軍以萬數，足以備用。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year Tutuha memorialized: "Qaračin troops number in the ten thousands— sufficient to prepare for use."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year Tutuha reported, "The Qaračin number in the ten thousands—enough for any task."

sentences.zh: 詔賜珠帽、珠衣、金帶、玉帶、海東青鶻各一，復賜其部曲毳衣、縑素萬匹。

translations.literal: An edict granted one pearl cap, pearl robe, gold belt, and jade belt each, and again granted his subordinates ten thousand pi of felt garments and plain silk.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted pearl cap and robe, gold and jade belts, and ten thousand bolts of felt and silk for his men.

sentences.zh: 於是率哈剌赤萬人北獵於漢塔海，邊寇聞之，皆引去。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led ten thousand Qaračin north to hunt at Hantaihai; border raiders, hearing of it, all withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He then led ten thousand Qaračin to hunt at Hantaihai; border raiders withdrew at the news.

sentences.zh: 二十九年秋，略地金山，獲海都之戶三千餘，還至和林。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the twenty-ninth year he raided territory at the Altai, obtained more than three thousand of Haidu's households, and returned to Karakorum.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the twenty-ninth year he raided the Altai, took more than three thousand of Haidu's households, and returned to Karakorum.

sentences.zh: 有詔進取乞裡吉思。

translations.literal: There was an edict to advance and take Kirghiz.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the conquest of Kirghiz.

sentences.zh: 三十年春，師次欠河，冰行數日，始至其境，盡收其五部之眾，屯兵守之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirtieth year the army halted at the Qian River; traveling on ice several days, they then reached its territory, fully received the multitudes of its five tribes, and garrisoned troops to hold them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirtieth year the army reached the Qian River, marched on ice for days, took all five Kirghiz tribes, and garrisoned them.

sentences.zh: 奏功，加龍虎衛上將軍，仍給行樞密院印。

translations.literal: Memorializing merit, he was promoted to General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and still granted the seal of the Mobile Military Affairs Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting his merit he was made General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and given the mobile military affairs seal.

sentences.zh: 海都聞取乞裡吉思，引兵至欠河，復敗之，擒其將孛羅察。

translations.literal: Haidu, hearing Kirghiz was taken, led troops to the Qian River and was again defeated; his general Bolochaq was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Haidu, hearing Kirghiz had fallen, came to the Qian River and was beaten again; his general Bolochaq was taken.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，成宗即位，詔以邊境事重，其免會朝，遣使就賜銀五百兩、七寶金壺盤盂各一、鈔萬貫、白氈帳一、獨峰駝五。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year Chengzong ascended the throne; an edict said that because frontier affairs were weighty, he was exempted from coming to court; envoys were sent to bestow five hundred taels of silver, one seven-jewel gold pot, basin, and bowl each, ten thousand strings of paper money, one white felt tent, and five Bactrian camels.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year Chengzong took the throne; frontier duty excused Tutuha from court; envoys brought five hundred taels of silver, jeweled gold vessels, ten thousand strings, a white felt tent, and five Bactrian camels.

sentences.zh: 冬，召至京師，賞賚有加，別賜其麾下士鈔千二百萬貫。

translations.literal: In winter he was summoned to the capital; rewards were increased; separately his subordinate soldiers were granted twelve million strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was summoned to the capital with added rewards; his soldiers received twelve million strings.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年春，仍出守北邊。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of Yuanzhen he again went out to guard the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of Yuanzhen 1 he returned to the northern frontier.

sentences.zh: 二年秋，諸王附海都者率眾來歸，邊民驚擾，身至玉龍罕界，饋餉安集之，導諸王岳木忽等入朝。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the second year, princes who had joined Haidu led multitudes to submit; border people were alarmed and disturbed; he personally went to the Yulonghan frontier, supplied food to settle them, and guided princes Uemuhu and others to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of Yuanzhen 2 princes who had sided with Haidu submitted in numbers; he went to the Yulonghan border in person, fed and settled the people, and escorted Prince Uemuhu and others to court.

sentences.zh: 帝解御衣以賜，又賜金五十兩、銀千五百兩、鈔五萬貫、轎輿各一。

translations.literal: The Emperor removed his own imperial robe to grant; again granted fifty taels of gold, fifteen hundred taels of silver, fifty thousand strings of paper money, and sedan chairs each one.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong gave his own robe from his shoulders plus fifty taels of gold, fifteen hundred of silver, fifty thousand strings, and a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 大德元年正月，拜銀青榮祿大夫、上柱國、同知樞密院事、欽察親軍都指揮使，奉命還北邊。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Dade he was appointed Silver-Green Glory Grand Master, Grand Preceptor of State, Vice Director of Military Affairs, and Commander-in-Chief of the Qipchaq Guard, ordered to return to the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Dade 1 he became Silver-Green Glory Grand Master, Grand Preceptor of State, Vice Director of Military Affairs, and Commander of the Qipchaq Guard, and returned north.

sentences.zh: 二月，至宣德府，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the second month he reached Xuande Prefecture and died at age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he reached Xuande Prefecture and died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫、司空，追封延國公，謚武毅，後加封升王。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Grand Master of the Purple-Gold Glory, Minister of Works; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Yan with posthumous title Wuyi; later further enfeoffed as Prince of Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously honored as Grand Master of Purple-Gold Glory and Minister of Works; enfeoffed Duke of Yan with posthumous title Wuyi; later raised to Prince of Sheng.

sentences.zh: 子八人，其第三子曰床兀兒。

translations.literal: He had eight sons; the third son was called Chüyü'er.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons; the third was Chüyü'er.

sentences.zh: 床兀兒初以大臣子奉詔從太師月兒魯行軍，戰於百塔山，有功，拜昭勇大將軍、左衛親軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Chüyü'er at first, as a minister's son by edict, followed Grand Preceptor Yelü Lü on campaign; fighting at Mount Baita he had merit; appointed General of Brilliant Courage and Left Commander of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Chüyü'er first followed Grand Preceptor Yelü Lü by imperial order; at Mount Baita he distinguished himself and became General of Brilliant Courage and Left Commander of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 大德元年，襲父職，領征北諸軍帥師逾金山，攻八鄰之地。

translations.literal: In the first year of Dade he inherited his father's post, leading the northern expedition armies across the Altai to attack the land of the Ba'arin.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 1 he succeeded his father, led the northern armies over the Altai against the Ba'arin.

sentences.zh: 八鄰之南有答魯忽河，其將帖良台阻水而軍，伐木柵岸以自庇，士皆下馬跪坐，持弓矢以待我軍，矢不能及，馬不能進。

translations.literal: South of the Ba'arin was the Tarluq River; its general Temürtei blocked the water and encamped; felling trees on the bank for palisades to shelter themselves, the soldiers all dismounted and knelt sitting, holding bow and arrow to await our army—arrows could not reach, horses could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: South of Ba'arin lay the Tarluq River; Temürtei camped behind it, felled bank timber for palisades, and had his men kneel with bows—arrows fell short and horses could not cross.

sentences.zh: 床兀兒命吹銅角，舉軍大呼，聲震林野。

translations.literal: Chüyü'er ordered the bronze horn blown; the whole army shouted; the sound shook forest and wild.
translations.idiomatic: Chüyü'er ordered the bronze horn sounded; the army roared until the woods shook.

sentences.zh: 其眾不知所為，爭起就馬。

translations.literal: Their multitude did not know what to do and competed to rise and mount horses.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy panicked and scrambled for their horses.

sentences.zh: 於是麾師畢渡，湧水拍岸，木柵漂散，因奮師馳擊，追奔五十里，盡得其人馬廬帳。

translations.literal: Thereupon he waved the army to finish crossing; surging water beat the banks; the wooden palisades drifted apart; accordingly he roused the army to gallop and strike; pursuing the rout fifty li, he fully obtained their men, horses, tents, and lodges.
translations.idiomatic: He then crossed in force; floodwater smashed the palisades; he charged, pursued fifty li, and took men, horses, and camps entire.

sentences.zh: 還次阿雷河，與海都所遣援八鄰之將孛伯軍遇。

translations.literal: Returning he halted at the Ale River and met Haidu's dispatched relief general for the Ba'arin, Boq's army.
translations.idiomatic: Returning he camped on the Ale River and met Boq, whom Haidu had sent to relieve the Ba'arin.

sentences.zh: 河之上有高山，孛伯陣於山上，馬不利下馳。

translations.literal: On the river was a high mountain; Boq arrayed on the mountain; horses were not suited to charging downhill.
translations.idiomatic: A high mountain overlooked the river; Boq formed on the heights where cavalry could not charge down.

sentences.zh: 床兀兒麾軍渡河蹙之，其馬多顛躓，急擊敗之，追奔三十餘里，孛伯僅以身免。

translations.literal: Chüyü'er waved the army to cross the river and press them; their horses mostly stumbled; pressing the attack he defeated them; pursuing the rout more than thirty li, Boq barely escaped with his body.
translations.idiomatic: Chüyü'er forced the crossing and closed on them; their horses stumbled; he routed them, pursued thirty li, and Boq alone escaped.

sentences.zh: 二年，北邊諸王都哇、徹徹禿等潛師襲火兒哈禿之地。

translations.literal: In the second year, northern princes Duwa, Chechektu, and others secretly led troops to raid the land of Qorqaz.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year princes Duwa and Chechektu secretly raided Qorqaz.

sentences.zh: 其地亦有山甚高，敵兵據之。

translations.literal: That land also had a mountain very high; enemy troops held it.
translations.idiomatic: There too a great height dominated the field; the enemy held it.

sentences.zh: 床兀兒選勇而善步者，持挺刃四面上，奮擊，盡覆其軍。

translations.literal: Chüyü'er selected the brave and those skilled at walking; holding clubs and blades they went up on four sides and struck fiercely; he fully overthrew their army.
translations.idiomatic: Chüyü'er picked brave footmen with clubs and blades, climbed on four sides, and overthrew the whole force.

sentences.zh: 三年，入朝，成宗親解御衣賜之，慰勞優渥，拜鎮國上將軍、僉樞密院事、欽察親軍都指揮使、太僕少卿。

translations.literal: In the third year he entered court; Chengzong personally removed his imperial robe to grant it; comfort and favor were generous; appointed General for Pacifying the State, Associate Director of Military Affairs, Commander-in-Chief of the Qipchaq Guard, and Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he came to court; Chengzong took off his own robe and gave it; he was made General for Pacifying the State, Associate Director of Military Affairs, Qipchaq Commander, and Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 復還邊。

translations.literal: He again returned to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 是時武宗在潛邸，領軍朔方，軍事必咨於床兀兒。

translations.literal: At that time Wuzong was at the Hidden Residence, commanding armies in the north; in military affairs he always consulted Chüyü'er.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong, still heir apparent in the north, always consulted Chüyü'er on military matters.

sentences.zh: 及戰，床兀兒嘗為先。

translations.literal: Whenever they fought, Chüyü'er always went first.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle Chüyü'er led the van.

sentences.zh: 四年秋，叛王禿麥、斡魯思等犯邊，床兀兒迎敵於闊客之地。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fourth year rebel princes Totoqmai and Olus and others violated the frontier; Chüyü'er met the enemy at Kuoke.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fourth year rebel princes Totoqmai and Olus invaded; Chüyü'er met them at Kuoke.

sentences.zh: 及其未陣，直前搏之，敵不敢支，追之，逾金山乃還。

translations.literal: Before they had formed battle lines he went straight forward to grapple them; the enemy could not hold; pursuing them, he crossed the Altai before returning.
translations.idiomatic: Before they could form he closed and grappled; they broke; he pursued beyond the Altai before turning back.

sentences.zh: 五年，海都兵越金山而南，止於鐵堅古山，因高以自保。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Haidu's troops crossed south of the Altai and halted at Mount Tiejianggu; relying on the heights they protected themselves.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Haidu crossed south of the Altai and held Mount Tiejianggu.

sentences.zh: 床兀兒急引兵敗之。

translations.literal: Chüyü'er urgently led troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Chüyü'er rushed up and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 復與都哇相持於兀兒禿之地。

translations.literal: Again he contended with Duwa at Urtu.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Duwa again at Urtu.

sentences.zh: 床兀兒以精銳馳其陣，左右奮擊，所殺不可勝計，都哇之兵幾盡。

translations.literal: Chüyü'er with elite troops galloped their formation; striking left and right with force, those killed were beyond counting; Duwa's army was nearly exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Chüyü'er drove elite horse into Duwa's line, struck both flanks, and slaughtered beyond count until Duwa's army nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 武宗親視其戰，乃嘆曰：「何其壯耶！

translations.literal: Wuzong personally viewed the battle and sighed: "How stalwart!
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong watched the fight and exclaimed, "How fierce!

sentences.zh: 力戰未有如此者。」

translations.literal: Never in fierce fighting has there been such as this."
translations.idiomatic: Never had he seen such fighting."

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔遣御史大夫禿只等即赤訥思之地集諸王軍將問戰勝功狀，咸稱床兀兒功第一。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict sent Censor-in-Chief Toci and others to Chinas to gather the princes' army generals and inquire into battle merit; all called Chüyü'er's merit first.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached court; Censor-in-Chief Toci was sent to Chinas to gather princes and generals on the victory; all ranked Chüyü'er first.

sentences.zh: 武宗既命尚雅忽禿楚王公主察吉兒，及使者以功簿奏，帝復出御衣遣使臨賜之。

translations.literal: Wuzong had already ordered Princess Chaji'er of the Prince of Chuyu'utu to be married, and when the envoy presented the merit register to memorialize, the Emperor again took out an imperial robe and sent an envoy to grant it in person.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong had already betrothed Princess Chaji'er of Chuyu'utu; when the merit rolls reached the throne, Chengzong again sent his own robe by envoy.

sentences.zh: 七年秋，入朝，帝親諭之曰：「卿鎮北邊，累建大功，雖以黃金周飾卿身，猶不足以盡朕意。」

translations.literal: In the autumn of the seventh year he entered court; the Emperor personally instructed him: "You guard the northern frontier and repeatedly establish great merit—though gold were wrapped around your body, it would still not exhaust Our intent."
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the seventh year he came to court; the Emperor told him, "You guard the north with repeated great deeds—even to gild your body would not repay Our debt."

sentences.zh: 賜以衣帽、金珠等物甚厚，拜驃騎衛上將軍、樞密院副使、欽察親軍都指揮使、太僕少卿，仍賜其軍萬人，鈔四千萬貫。

translations.literal: Granted hats, robes, gold, pearls, and other things very generously; appointed General of the Swift-Cavalry Guard, Vice Director of Military Affairs, Commander-in-Chief of the Qipchaq Guard, and Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud; still granted ten thousand troops to his army and forty million strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: He received rich gifts of hat, robe, gold, and pearls; was made General of the Swift-Cavalry Guard, Vice Director of Military Affairs, Qipchaq Commander, and Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud; ten thousand troops and forty million strings went to his command.

sentences.zh: 九年，諸王都哇、察八兒、明裡帖木兒等相聚而謀曰：「昔我太祖艱難以成帝業，奄有天下，我子孫乃弗克靖恭，以安享其成，連年構兵，以相殘殺，是自隳祖宗之業也。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the princes Duwa, Chabai, and Minglitaimur and others gathered to deliberate: "In old times our Grand Ancestor with hardship completed the imperial enterprise and suddenly possessed All-under-Heaven; we his descendants have been unable to maintain reverent peace and peacefully enjoy its completion—year after year raising armies to slaughter one another; this is ourselves destroying the ancestors' enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year princes Duwa, Chabai, and Minglitaimur met and said, "Genghis won the realm through hardship; we his heirs cannot keep the peace but war among ourselves—we ruin his legacy.

sentences.zh: 今撫軍鎮邊者，皆吾世祖之嫡孫，吾與誰爭哉？

translations.literal: Now those who pacify the army and guard the frontier are all direct grandsons of our Shizu—whom shall we contend with?
translations.idiomatic: Those who hold the frontier now are Kublai's own grandsons—with whom should we fight?

sentences.zh: 且前與土土哈戰既弗能勝，今與其子床兀兒戰又無功，惟天惟祖宗意可見矣。

translations.literal: Moreover before, fighting Tutuha we could not win; now fighting his son Chüyü'er again without merit—Heaven's and the ancestors' intent can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: We could not beat Tutuha; we cannot beat his son Chüyü'er—the will of Heaven and the ancestors is plain.

sentences.zh: 不若遣使請命罷兵，通一家之好，使吾士民老者得以養，少者得以長，傷殘疲憊者得以休息，則亦無負太祖之所望於我子孫者矣。」

translations.literal: Better to send envoys to request orders to cease arms and open one family's good relations, so that our scholars and people—the old may be nourished, the young may grow, the wounded, crippled, weary, and exhausted may rest—then we also will not fail what the Grand Ancestor hoped for in us his descendants."
translations.idiomatic: Better to sue for peace and restore kinship, so old and young may thrive and the maimed rest—we would not betray what Genghis wished for his line."

sentences.zh: 使至，帝許之。

translations.literal: When the envoys arrived, the Emperor permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When their envoys came, the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是明裡帖木兒等罷兵入朝，特為置驛以通往來。

translations.literal: Thereupon Minglitaimur and the others ceased arms and entered court; specially post stations were established to facilitate coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Minglitaimur and the others laid down arms and came to court; relay stations were set up for their traffic.

sentences.zh: 十年，拜榮祿大夫、同知樞密院事，尋拜光祿大夫、知樞密院事，欽察左衛指揮、太僕少卿皆如故。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was appointed Glory Grand Master and Vice Director of Military Affairs; soon appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Director of Military Affairs; Qipchaq Left Guard Commander and Vice Minister of the Imperial Stud remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he became Glory Grand Master and Vice Director of Military Affairs; soon Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Director of Military Affairs, retaining the Qipchaq Left Guard and Imperial Stud posts.

sentences.zh: 子六人：燕帖木兒，答剌罕、太師、右丞相、太平王；

translations.literal: He had six sons: Yanztemür, Daraqan, Grand Preceptor, Right Chancellor, Prince of Taiping;
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Yanztemür, Daraqan, Grand Preceptor, Right Chancellor, and Prince of Taiping;

sentences.zh: 撒敦，左丞相；

translations.literal: Sadun, Left Chancellor;
translations.idiomatic: Sadun, Left Chancellor;

sentences.zh: 答裡，襲封句容郡王。

translations.literal: Dali, inheriting enfeoffment as Prince of Jurong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Dali, who inherited the enfeoffment as Prince of Jurong Commandery.
